d.how: For each cup, grind 18g espresso beans fine and pull a short double, about 25g in the cup. Make four, using 72g beans, and serve each with a small glass of water.

s.note: Hard pretzels with hot mustard cheddar dip.
s.how: Warm 150ml evaporated milk in a small pan and stir in 200g grated cheddar over low heat until smooth. Add 1 tsp Dijon mustard and a pinch of cayenne. Serve hot in a bowl with 200g hard pretzels.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork dumplings with soy, vinegar and ginger dip.
s.how: Fry 24 frozen pork dumplings flat side down in 1 tbsp oil for 2 minutes, add 120ml water, cover and steam 4 minutes, then fry again until crisp underneath. Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp black vinegar and 1 tbsp fine ginger matchsticks for dipping.

m.note: Griddle-chopped beef and onion with melted cheese in a hero.
m.how: Fry 1 diced onion on a hot griddle, add 600g beef mince and chop it up with a spatula as it browns, seasoning well. Lay 6 slices American cheese on top and chop through until melted. Pile into 4 toasted hero rolls with shredded lettuce, sliced tomato and mayo.

w.note: Chocolate layer cake in chocolate buttercream, with candles.
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g caster sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 220g self-raising flour, 40g cocoa and 120ml milk. Bake in two 20cm tins at 180C for 25 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar and 40g cocoa, sandwich and cover the cakes, and add birthday candles.

d.note: Drip coffee with milk and sugar in paper cups.
d.how: Brew 1 litre of drip coffee with 60g ground coffee. Pour into four paper cups with milk, about 200ml in total, and sugar to taste, and serve fast.

s.note: Thick beer-battered onion rings fried until puffed.
s.how: Slice 2 large brown onions into thick rings and soak in 250ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Whisk 150g plain flour with 200ml lager and a pinch of salt. Dip the rings in the batter and fry at 185C for 2 minutes until puffed and golden. Salt straight away.

s.note: Double-fried chips with hot brown gravy.
s.how: Fry 1kg potatoes cut into chips at 140C for 6 minutes, rest, then at 185C until crisp. Cook 30g butter and 2 tbsp flour until nut brown, whisk in 400ml beef stock and simmer 5 minutes, seasoning well. Pour the gravy over the chips.

m.note: Beef patty on rye with Swiss and slow onions, griddled in butter.
m.how: Cook 2 sliced brown onions in butter over low heat for 25 minutes. Shape 600g beef mince into 4 thin oval patties and sear 2 minutes a side. Butter 8 slices rye bread on the outside, fill each sandwich with a patty, onions and 2 slices Swiss cheese, and griddle in butter until crisp and melted.

w.note: Lattice-topped Granny Smith apple pie with cinnamon and sugar.
w.how: Peel and slice 1kg Granny Smith apples and toss with 100g caster sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 2 tbsp flour. Line a pie dish with 1 sheet sweet shortcrust, fill, and weave a lattice from a second sheet. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes until golden and bubbling.

d.note: Piña colada blended icy with a cocktail umbrella.
d.how: For four drinks, blend 200ml white rum, 240ml pineapple juice and 160ml coconut cream with 4 cups of ice until smooth. Pour into tall glasses and add a cocktail umbrella.

s.note: Pale buttery shortbread fingers wrapped in a napkin.
s.how: Beat 250g soft butter with 100g icing sugar, then mix in 350g plain flour to a soft dough. Press into a lined 20 by 30cm tin, prick all over and score into fingers. Bake at 160C for 25 minutes until pale gold. Cut while warm and wrap in a napkin.

s.note: Warm salted dry-roasted peanuts in little paper packets.
s.how: Toss 300g dry-roasted peanuts with 1 tsp brown sugar and 1/2 tsp fine salt. Warm on a tray at 170C for 5 minutes, cool slightly and spoon into small paper packets like the ones on the plane.

m.note: Apple, celery, grapes and walnuts in creamy lemon dressing on butter lettuce.
m.how: Toast 80g walnuts. Dice 2 apples and 3 celery sticks and halve 200g grapes. Mix 100g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp crème fraîche and the juice of half a lemon, fold everything through and season. Spoon onto leaves of 1 butter lettuce.

w.note: Baked New York cheesecake topped with strawberries.
w.how: Crush 200g digestive biscuits with 80g melted butter and press into a 22cm tin. Beat 750g cream cheese with 200g caster sugar, 200g sour cream and 3 eggs until smooth. Pour over and bake in a water bath at 150C for 70 minutes, then cool in the oven and chill overnight. Top with 250g sliced strawberries.

d.note: Gin and dry vermouth stirred cold in frozen glasses with an olive.
d.how: Freeze four martini glasses for 30 minutes. For each drink, stir 60ml gin with 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds and strain into a frozen glass with a green olive. Makes four with 240ml gin.

s.note: King prawns on iceberg with a tangy cocktail sauce and lemon.
s.how: Peel 500g cooked king prawns. Mix 120g mayonnaise, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, a squeeze of lemon and a dash of hot sauce. Shred half an iceberg lettuce into four glasses, pile on the prawns, spoon over the sauce and hang a lemon wedge on each rim.

s.note: Puff pastry cases filled with creamy chicken, mushroom and tarragon.
s.how: Cut 16 rounds from 2 sheets puff pastry, press a smaller ring into each and bake at 200C for 12 minutes, then push down the centres. Fry 250g diced chicken thighs and 150g chopped mushrooms in butter, add 200ml cream, 1 tbsp chopped tarragon and a squeeze of lemon and simmer until thick. Fill the cases and warm through for 3 minutes.

m.note: Crisp battered sweet and sour pork with pineapple and capsicum, with rice.
m.how: Cut 600g pork shoulder into cubes, toss in 1 tbsp soy, then in 80g cornflour, and fry at 180C until crisp. In a wok, fry 1 red capsicum and 200g pineapple pieces for 2 minutes, add 3 tbsp white vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp tomato sauce and 100ml water and thicken with 1 tsp cornflour. Toss the pork through and serve with 400g steamed jasmine rice.

w.note: Vanilla butter cake with raspberry jam and buttercream under white fondant.
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 250g caster sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 300g self-raising flour with 125ml milk. Bake in two 20cm tins at 165C for 35 minutes and cool. Sandwich with 150g raspberry jam and buttercream of 150g butter and 300g icing sugar, coat thinly, then cover with 500g rolled white fondant and add a few fresh flowers. Serve in fingers.

d.note: Rum, pineapple, coconut and lime blended with ice under an umbrella.
d.how: For four drinks, blend 180ml white rum, 120ml pineapple juice, 120ml coconut cream and 60ml lime juice with 4 cups of ice until smooth. Pour into tall glasses and add a cocktail umbrella to each, like the island resort.

s.note: Mixed nuts roasted in honey, sugar and cinnamon.
s.how: Toss 300g mixed nuts with 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Spread on a lined tray and roast at 170C for 15 minutes, stirring halfway. Keep stirring as they cool so they don't clump.

s.note: Shortbread rounds with a cut-out middle, brushed with edible gold.
s.how: Beat 200g soft butter with 100g icing sugar and mix in 300g plain flour to a dough. Roll 5mm thick, cut rounds the size of a subway token and cut a small hole from the middle of each. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes and cool. Brush with edible gold dust mixed with a drop of water.

m.note: Chicken thighs on saffron-gold rice with sofrito, olives and capers.
m.how: Brown 800g chicken thighs and set aside. Fry 1 onion, 1 capsicum, 3 garlic cloves and a handful of coriander until soft, add 1 tsp ground annatto, 300g long grain rice, 60g green olives, 1 tbsp capers and 650ml chicken stock. Sit the chicken on top, cover and cook on low for 25 minutes until the rice is tender.

w.note: Butter cake buried under a thick cinnamon crumble.
w.how: Rub 100g plain flour, 100g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 80g cold butter into big crumbs. Beat 125g butter with 125g caster sugar, add 2 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour with 100ml milk. Spread in a lined 20cm tin, cover with the crumble and bake at 180C for 40 minutes.

d.note: Cold tallboy lagers, each wrapped in a brown paper bag.
d.how: Chill four 700ml tallboy cans of lager for at least 3 hours. Slide each into a brown paper bag, fold the top down around the can and hand them out on the subway platform.

s.note: Cherry tomatoes filled with basil and lemon whipped feta.
s.how: Cut the tops off 24 cherry tomatoes and scoop out the seeds. Blitz 150g feta with a handful of basil, the zest of 1 lemon and 2 tbsp olive oil until smooth. Pipe into the tomatoes and top each with a small basil leaf. A red nose for every guest.

s.note: Butter-roasted peanuts with chilli and smoked paprika.
s.how: Melt 20g butter and toss through 300g salted peanuts with 1/2 tsp chilli flakes and 1 tsp smoked paprika. Spread on a tray and roast at 170C for 10 minutes. Cool for 5 minutes and serve in small bowls.

m.note: Turkey and Swiss kaiser rolls wrapped tight in paper.
m.how: Split 4 kaiser rolls, spread with 80g mayonnaise and 1 tbsp mustard. Fill with 400g sliced turkey, 8 slices Swiss cheese, shredded iceberg lettuce and 2 sliced tomatoes, and season with salt and pepper. Wrap each tightly in paper and cut in half.

w.note: Jam sponge in white buttercream with a piped clown face and cherry nose.
w.how: Split a 400g sponge cake and fill with 100g raspberry jam. Beat 200g butter with 400g icing sugar and spread all over the cake. Tint a little leftover buttercream and pipe a clown face on top, then press a maraschino cherry in for the nose.

d.note: Cold lager in plastic cups, a toast to leaving New York.
d.how: Chill four 375ml bottles of lager in the fridge for at least two hours. Pour into plastic cups and toast to finally getting out of New York, before anything else goes wrong.

s.note: Hot pink beetroot and feta dip with warm flatbread.
s.how: Wrap 2 beetroots in foil and roast at 200C for 1 hour, then peel. Blitz with 100g feta, 150g Greek yoghurt, 1 garlic clove, the juice of half a lemon and a little dill until bright pink and smooth. Serve with 4 warm flatbreads cut into wedges.

s.note: Crisp crumpets with honey butter, cut into quarters.
s.how: Beat 60g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of salt. Toast 8 crumpets until the holes are crisp, spread with the honey butter while hot so it runs into the holes, and cut into quarters.

m.note: Beef goulash with sweet paprika and caraway, on egg noodles with sour cream.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Cook 3 sliced brown onions slowly for 20 minutes, add 2 tbsp sweet paprika, a pinch of hot paprika and 1 tsp caraway seeds, then 400g crushed tomatoes, 300ml beef stock and the beef. Braise at 160C for 2.5 hours. Serve over 400g egg noodles with 150g sour cream.

w.note: Wobbly pink lemonade jelly with raspberries set inside.
w.how: Soak 8 gelatine leaves in cold water. Warm 300ml of 1 litre pink lemonade, squeeze the gelatine and stir in until melted, then add the rest of the lemonade. Pour into a jelly mould with 125g raspberries and set 6 hours. Dip in hot water, turn out and put on something upbeat.

d.note: Pink lemonade over ice with a scoop of raspberry sorbet.
d.how: Put a scoop of raspberry sorbet in each of four tall glasses, about 400ml in total. Pour chilled pink lemonade slowly over the top, about 250ml a glass, so it fizzes up pink. Serve with a spoon and a straw.

s.note: Cheddar, brie and blue with crackers, grapes and fig paste.
s.how: Take 150g aged cheddar, 150g brie and 120g blue cheese out of the fridge an hour before serving. Arrange on a board with 150g crackers, a bunch of grapes and 100g fig paste.

s.note: Crisp bagel chips with chive and lemon cream cheese.
s.how: Slice 3 day-old bagels into thin rounds, brush with 2 tbsp olive oil and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until crisp. Beat 250g cream cheese with 2 tbsp chopped chives and the zest of 1 lemon. Serve the chips around the schmear.

m.note: Sliced sirloin, slow onions and melted Swiss on sourdough with horseradish mayo.
m.how: Cook 2 sliced brown onions in butter over low heat for 30 minutes. Sear 600g sirloin steak hard for 3 minutes a side, rest and slice thin. Mix 80g mayonnaise with 1 tbsp horseradish. Toast 8 slices sourdough, spread with the mayo, pile on steak and onions, lay 4 slices Swiss cheese on top and grill until melted.

w.note: Smooth homemade vanilla custard, warm or chilled.
w.how: Heat 500ml milk with a split vanilla bean until steaming. Whisk 4 egg yolks with 60g caster sugar and 2 tbsp cornflour, pour on the hot milk, then return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick. Serve warm, or chill with plastic pressed on the surface.

d.n: Warm milk or a cold beer
d.note: Honey nutmeg milk for the baby schedule, cold lager for the dads.
d.how: Warm 500ml full cream milk with 1 tbsp honey and a pinch of nutmeg for anyone keeping the baby's hours. For the three dads, chill 3 bottles of lager and serve ice cold.

s.note: Little glazed meatloaf balls, sticky with tomato sauce and brown sugar.
s.how: Soak 40g breadcrumbs in 60ml milk, then mix lightly with 500g beef mince, half a grated brown onion, 1 egg and salt. Roll into 20 balls and bake at 200C for 15 minutes. Mix 4 tbsp tomato sauce with 1 tbsp brown sugar, brush over and bake 5 minutes more.

s.note: Prosciutto wrapped in a criss-cross around breadsticks, with whipped ricotta.
s.how: Cut 100g prosciutto into long thin strips and wind them criss-cross around 16 breadsticks like fishnet. Stand them up in a tall glass. Whip 200g ricotta with a pinch of salt and pepper and serve in a small bowl beside them.

m.note: Crisp shredded duck in pancakes with cucumber, spring onion and hoisin.
m.how: Salt 4 duck legs and leave uncovered in the fridge overnight. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes until crisp, then shred. Steam 20 Chinese pancakes for 3 minutes. Serve with 1 Lebanese cucumber and 4 spring onions cut into matchsticks and 120ml hoisin sauce for rolling at the table.

w.note: Star and tree sugar cookies iced in bright colours.
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 120g caster sugar, add 1 egg and 1 tsp vanilla, then mix in 280g plain flour. Chill 30 minutes, roll 5mm thick, cut stars and trees and bake at 180C for 8 minutes. Mix 250g icing sugar with a little water and food colouring and ice the cooled cookies.

d.note: Frothy chocolate malted milk blended with vanilla ice cream.
d.how: Whisk 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 2 tbsp cocoa into 800ml cold milk. Blend with 4 scoops vanilla ice cream, about 300ml, until frothy. Pour into four tall glasses.

s.note: Extra green guacamole with lime, coriander and spinach, with corn chips.
s.how: Blitz a handful of baby spinach with the juice of 2 limes until smooth. Mash 3 avocados with the spinach, a handful of chopped coriander, 1 chopped jalapeño and salt until slimy green. Serve with 300g corn chips.

s.note: Mini pizzas with a pepperoni grate across the top.
s.how: Roll 500g pizza dough thin and cut 12 rounds. Spread with pizza sauce, using 150ml, and top with 150g grated mozzarella. Slice 80g pepperoni into thin strips and lay them in a crosshatch like a manhole grate. Bake at 230C for 8 minutes.

m.note: Hearty beef and vegetable stew with crusty bread.
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 2 chopped brown onions, 3 carrots, 2 celery sticks and 2 tbsp tomato paste and cook 5 minutes, then 1 litre beef stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 2.5 hours, adding 600g potatoes in chunks for the last hour. Serve with a loaf of Italian bread.

w.note: Dense chocolate mud cake under dragged dark ganache.
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 200g butter. Whisk in 300g caster sugar and 4 eggs, then fold in 150g plain flour and 30g cocoa. Bake in a lined 22cm tin at 160C for 70 minutes and cool. Melt 150g dark chocolate with 150ml cream, pour over and drag with a fork like sewer muck.

d.note: Lime cordial and tonic that glows under a black light.
d.how: Pour 40ml lime cordial into each of four tall glasses over ice and top with tonic water, about 250ml each. Tonic glows blue-white under a black light, so switch the lights off.

s.note: Lemony lobster salad piled on toasted buttered brioche rounds.
s.how: Chop 300g cooked lobster meat and fold with 3 tbsp mayonnaise, the juice of half a lemon, 1 finely diced celery stick and chopped chives. Cut 16 rounds from buttered brioche slices and toast. Pile the lobster on top.

s.note: Cheddar, colby and squeaky curds with crackers, apple and mustard.
s.how: Take 150g aged cheddar, 150g colby cheese and 150g cheese curds out of the fridge an hour ahead. Arrange with 150g crackers, 2 sliced apples and a small pot of grainy mustard.

m.note: Steamed pastrami piled on soft white bread with mayo, lettuce and tomato.
m.how: Steam 500g sliced pastrami for 10 minutes until glossy. Spread 8 slices soft white bread with 80g mayonnaise, add shredded iceberg lettuce and 2 sliced tomatoes, and pile the pastrami high. Alvy would want rye and mustard, so have them on the side.

w.note: Tall baked lemon cheesecake on a biscuit base.
w.how: Crush 200g digestive biscuits with 80g melted butter and press into a 22cm tin. Beat 900g cream cheese with 220g caster sugar, 200g sour cream, 4 eggs and the zest of 1 lemon. Pour over and bake in a water bath at 150C for 70 minutes. Cool in the oven, then chill overnight.

d.note: Sparkling water with lemon, cucumber and mint over ice.
d.how: Fill a big jug with ice, a sliced lemon, half a sliced cucumber and a handful of mint. Top with 1.5 litres chilled sparkling water and pour into four glasses, the closest thing to his alfalfa sprouts order.

s.note: Chunky green guacamole with lime, coriander and chilli, with corn chips.
s.how: Mash 3 avocados with the juice of 2 limes and salt. Fold in half a finely diced red onion, a handful of chopped coriander and 1 chopped red chilli. Press plastic wrap on the surface until serving so it stays green. Serve with 300g corn chips.

s.note: Oversized pizza dough knots in garlic butter and parmesan.
s.how: Cut 500g pizza dough into 8 thick strips, tie each into a big knot and prove 30 minutes. Bake at 230C for 15 minutes. Melt 50g butter with 3 crushed garlic cloves, brush over the hot knots and shower with 30g grated parmesan.

m.note: Thin pizza with pepperoni, fresh pineapple and jalapeño.
m.how: Rest 2 balls of pizza dough, about 500g, at room temperature for an hour. Stretch thin, spread with 200ml pizza sauce and top with 250g grated mozzarella, 100g pepperoni, 200g fresh pineapple pieces and 1 sliced jalapeño. Bake on a preheated tray at the oven's highest setting for 8 minutes.

w.note: Thick green mint choc chip milkshake.
w.how: Blend 12 scoops mint choc chip ice cream, about 750ml, with 800ml cold full cream milk until thick and smooth. Pour into four chilled tall glasses and serve with straws.

d.note: Lime cordial and soda over ice with a lime wheel.
d.how: Pour 40ml lime cordial into each of four tall glasses packed with ice. Top with soda water, about 250ml each, and hang a lime wheel on the rim.

s.note: Almond-stuffed prunes wrapped in crisp streaky bacon.
s.how: Push an almond into each of 20 pitted prunes. Wrap each in half a rasher of streaky bacon, using 10 rashers, and secure with a toothpick. Bake at 200C for 15 minutes until the bacon is crisp. Serve warm.

s.note: Icy orange juice slush with a splash of vodka.
s.how: Blend 500ml orange juice with 2 cups ice and 80ml vodka until slushy. Pour into shot glasses and serve straight away, before the market closes. Leave out the vodka for anyone not drinking.

m.note: Slow-roasted rib roast with jus, horseradish cream and potatoes.
m.how: Salt a 2kg standing rib roast the day before and leave uncovered in the fridge. Roast at 120C until 52C inside, about 2.5 hours, rest 30 minutes, then blast at 260C for 8 minutes for a crust. Simmer the pan juices with 300ml beef stock for jus. Serve with 150g horseradish cream and 1kg roast potatoes.

w.note: Orange butter cake soaked in a sticky orange glaze.
w.how: Beat 200g butter, 200g caster sugar and the zest of 2 oranges, add 3 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour with 100ml orange juice. Bake in a lined tin at 170C for 45 minutes. Boil 100ml orange juice concentrate with 50g sugar for 3 minutes and brush over the warm cake.

d.note: Fresh orange juice and chilled sparkling wine in flutes.
d.how: Squeeze 4 oranges, about 300ml juice, and chill well. Fill four flutes halfway with the juice and gently top with chilled sparkling wine, about 300ml in total, pouring slowly so it does not foam over.

s.note: Sage and apple sausage rolls, golden and flaky, with hot mustard
s.how: Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 grated apple, 1 finely chopped onion and 6 chopped sage leaves. Lay along 2 sheets of puff pastry, roll up, egg wash, score, cut into 16 and bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with mustard.

s.note: Sharp cheddar and Red Leicester with pickled onions and chutney
s.how: Take 200g vintage cheddar and 200g Red Leicester out of the fridge an hour ahead. Cut into wedges and arrange on a wooden board with pickled onions, a bowl of apple chutney and a stack of oatcakes.

m.note: Crisp goose legs, goose fat potatoes, red cabbage and apple sauce
m.how: Salt 4 goose legs overnight. Roast at 170C for 2 hours until crisp, pouring off the fat. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in that fat at 200C for 45 minutes. Braise half a red cabbage with 2 sliced apples and 3 tbsp red wine vinegar for an hour.

w.note: Brandy-soaked fruit pudding, steamed, flamed at the table, brandy custard
w.how: Soak 500g dried fruit in 100ml brandy overnight. Mix with 125g soft butter, 125g brown sugar, 2 eggs, 100g breadcrumbs, 75g flour and 2 tsp mixed spice. Steam in a greased basin for 4 hours. Warm 2 tbsp brandy, light it and pour over at the table. Serve with custard.

d.note: Port and red wine warmed with clove-studded roasted oranges
d.how: Stud 2 oranges with cloves and roast at 180C for 30 minutes. Warm 375ml port and 375ml red wine gently with the oranges, 2 cinnamon sticks and 2 tbsp sugar for 20 minutes, never boiling. Ladle into four cups.

s.note: Charred baby corn with butter, chilli and lime salt
s.how: Blanch 400g baby corn in salted boiling water for 2 minutes and drain well. Char on a hot griddle for 3 minutes with 30g butter, then sprinkle with chilli flakes, lime zest and salt. Serve with lime wedges and eat it like a cob.

s.note: Crème fraîche, salmon roe and chives on water crackers
s.how: Spread 20 water crackers with a teaspoon of crème fraîche each, about 200ml in total. Top each with half a teaspoon of salmon roe and a few snipped chives. Assemble just before serving so the crackers stay crisp and Josh can spit one out.

m.note: Griddled franks with mustard, sauerkraut and red onion sauce
m.how: Simmer 8 franks in water with half an onion for 5 minutes, then griddle until blistered. Soften 2 sliced onions in oil for 15 minutes, add 2 tbsp tomato paste and a splash of vinegar. Steam 8 buns, fill and top with mustard and sauerkraut.

w.note: One huge soft cookie with piano keys piped on top
w.how: Brown 150g butter and cool. Beat with 200g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour, half a tsp bicarb and 200g choc chips. Press into a pizza tray and bake at 180C for 18 minutes. Cool and pipe white icing piano keys across it.

d.note: Root beer poured slowly over two scoops of vanilla ice cream
d.how: Chill four tall glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Add two scoops of vanilla ice cream to each, then pour 375ml root beer slowly down the side so it foams up. Serve with long spoons and straws.

s.note: Toasted bagels, whipped cream cheese, lox, capers and red onion
s.how: Whip 250g cream cheese with a splash of milk until light. Split and toast 4 bagels. Spread thickly, then layer with 200g smoked salmon, a few capers, paper-thin red onion and dill sprigs. Cut in half and serve on a board.

s.note: Dark smoky popcorn with flaky salt, like stars in a night sky
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil in a large pot with 3 kernels. When they pop, add 120g kernels, cover and shake until the popping slows. Toss with 50g melted butter, flaky salt and 1 tsp smoked paprika.

m.note: Kung pao chicken and rice, eaten from the cartons
m.how: Marinate 700g diced chicken thigh in 2 tbsp soy and 1 tbsp cornflour. Fry hot with 10 dried chillies and 1 tsp Sichuan pepper. Add sauce of 2 tbsp black vinegar, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp sugar and 2 tbsp Shaoxing, then 80g peanuts and spring onion. Serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.note: Soft vanilla cookies iced half vanilla, half chocolate
w.how: Beat 115g butter with 150g sugar, 1 egg and 80g sour cream, then fold in 250g flour and 1 tsp baking powder. Scoop 8 large mounds and bake at 180C for 12 minutes. Ice the flat sides, half with vanilla icing and half with icing mixed with cocoa.

d.note: Rye, sweet vermouth and bitters, stirred cold, with a cherry
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml rye, 30ml sweet vermouth and 2 dashes aromatic bitters over plenty of ice for 30 seconds. Strain into a chilled coupe and drop in a cocktail cherry. Makes four, so make them one or two at a time.

s.note: Thick double-fried chips with salt and white vinegar
s.how: Cut 1kg russets into thick chips, rinse and dry well. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes, rest 20 minutes, then fry again at 185C until crisp and golden. Salt hard and put a shaker of white vinegar on the table.

s.note: Saltines, sharp cheddar slabs, pickle spears and hot mustard
s.how: Take 250g sharp cheddar out of the fridge an hour ahead and cut into thick slabs. Cut 4 dill pickles into spears. Lay out with a sleeve of saltine crackers and a small dish of hot English mustard for smearing.

m.note: Double smashed patties, American cheese, iceberg, onion and pickle
m.how: Roll 800g beef mince into 8 balls. Smash thin on a smoking flat-top, salt, flip at 90 seconds and add a slice of American cheese. Stack two per toasted bun with shredded iceberg, diced onion and pickles.

w.note: Buttered bread layered with brandied peaches, baked in custard
w.how: Soak 2 drained tins of sliced peaches in 3 tbsp brandy and 2 tbsp brown sugar. Butter 8 slices of thick white bread and layer with the peaches. Pour over 4 eggs whisked with 500ml milk and vanilla, rest 20 minutes and bake at 170C for 40 minutes.

d.note: Strong drip coffee poured into heavy diner mugs all night
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine. Keep the pot on the hot plate and pour into heavy mugs, black, topping up whenever anyone's cup gets low. Brew a second pot if the movie runs late.

s.note: Egg and cress and cucumber sandwiches, crusts off, in triangles
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, mash with 2 tbsp mayo and a handful of cress. Spread 150g cream cheese on bread and layer with thin cucumber. Use 12 slices soft white bread in total, cut off the crusts and cut into triangles.

s.note: Seeded crackers with whipped feta and roasted capsicum dip
s.how: Roast 2 red capsicums at 220C for 30 minutes, peel and seed. Blitz with 200g feta, 150g Greek yoghurt and a pinch of chilli flakes until smooth. Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with oil and serve with seeded crackers.

m.note: Lemon butter roast chicken with potatoes roasted in the fat
m.how: Dry-brine a 1.8kg chicken overnight. Push 50g butter mixed with lemon zest and thyme under the skin. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes then 180C for 50 minutes, with 1kg halved potatoes in the tray. Rest 15 minutes before carving.

w.note: Cream scones split and filled with strawberries and whipped cream
w.how: Mix 300g self-raising flour with 200ml cream and 2 tbsp sugar to a soft dough. Pat out, cut 4 rounds and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Toss 500g sliced strawberries with 2 tbsp sugar. Whip 200ml cream softly, split the scones and fill.

d.note: Strong sweet black tea over ice with lemon and mint
d.how: Steep 6 black tea bags in 1L just-boiled water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 80g sugar while hot. Chill completely. Pour over ice in four tall glasses with lemon slices and a sprig of mint in each.

s.note: Thick buttermilk onion rings in panko with smoky barbecue mayo
s.how: Cut 3 brown onions into thick rings and soak in 300ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Dredge in flour, dip in 2 beaten eggs and press into panko. Fry at 180C for 2 minutes until deep golden. Mix 100g mayo with 3 tbsp barbecue sauce to dip.

s.note: Baked spinach and artichoke dip, bubbling, with corn chips
s.how: Wilt 250g spinach, squeeze dry and chop. Mix with 1 jar chopped artichoke hearts, 250g cream cheese, 100g sour cream, 50g parmesan and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Top with 100g mozzarella and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling. Serve with corn chips.

m.note: Slow-braised beef stew turned green with peas and spinach
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 onions, 3 garlic cloves and 2 celery sticks. Add 250ml red wine and 500ml stock, cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours. Stir in 200g peas and 100g spinach at the end. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Fluffy buttermilk waffles with cream, strawberries and maple syrup
w.how: Whisk 250g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 400ml buttermilk, 2 yolks and 80g melted butter. Whip 2 whites to soft peaks and fold through. Cook in a hot waffle iron until crisp. Serve with whipped cream, 250g strawberries and maple syrup.

d.note: Green apple, cucumber, lime and mint blitzed into a slushy
d.how: Core and chop 3 green apples and 1 cucumber. Blitz with the juice of 3 limes, a big handful of mint, 2 tbsp honey and 2 cups of ice until slushy. Pour into four glasses and serve straight away with a mint sprig.

s.note: Fresh oysters on ice with lemon and shallot mignonette
s.how: Finely dice 2 shallots and mix with 80ml red wine vinegar and plenty of cracked pepper. Rest 20 minutes. Lay 24 freshly shucked oysters on crushed ice, with lemon wedges and the mignonette in a small bowl with a spoon.

s.note: Beer-battered flathead and chips in paper cones with tartare
s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 50g cornflour and 300ml cold lager to a batter. Cut 600g potatoes into chips and fry twice. Dip 500g flathead strips in batter and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Serve in paper cones with tartare and lemon.

m.note: Boiled lobster, split and grilled with garlic butter
m.how: Cook 2 raw lobsters, about 800g each, in boiling salted water for 8 minutes per 500g. Split lengthways, crack the claws and brush the flesh with 100g butter melted with 3 garlic cloves. Grill flesh-side up for 2 minutes. Serve with drawn butter and lemon.

w.note: Blue jelly over coconut panna cotta with gummy fish on top
w.how: Bloom 3 gelatine leaves and stir into 400ml warm coconut milk with 60g sugar. Set in four glasses for 2 hours. Steep 10 butterfly pea flowers in 400ml hot water with 60g sugar, add 3 more gelatine leaves, cool and pour over. Set, then add gummy fish.

d.note: Vodka, blue curaçao and lemonade over ice with lemon
d.how: For each drink, fill a tall glass with ice and add 30ml vodka and 20ml blue curaçao. Top with about 150ml lemonade and stir gently. Garnish with a lemon wheel. Makes four, so mix them one at a time.

s.note: Mini pepperoni pizzas on rounds of dough, hot from the oven
s.how: Roll out 500g pizza dough and cut into 16 rounds. Spread each with a spoon of pizza sauce, then add grated mozzarella and a slice of pepperoni. Bake on a hot tray at 230C for 8 minutes until the bases are crisp and the cheese bubbles.

s.note: Brown butter cookies with little pug faces in chocolate
s.how: Brown 125g butter and cool. Beat with 150g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 200g flour and half a tsp bicarb. Roll into 16 balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Cool, then pipe pug faces on with 50g melted dark chocolate.

m.note: Thin crust pizza with crushed tomato, mozzarella and sausage
m.how: Stretch 2 balls of cold-fermented dough, 500g in total, thin. Spread with 200g crushed tomato seasoned with salt. Top with 250g low-moisture mozzarella and 3 Italian sausages, skins off, crumbled. Bake on a steel at max heat for 7 minutes.

w.note: Cake pops dipped in white chocolate and brushed silver
w.how: Crumble a 500g butter cake and mix with 100g cream cheese icing until it holds together. Roll into 16 balls, push in sticks and chill an hour. Dip in 300g melted white chocolate, set, then brush with silver lustre dust.

d.note: Very sweet lemonade, the alien drink of choice
d.how: Make a syrup of 150g caster sugar dissolved in 150ml hot water and cool. Stir with the juice of 4 lemons and 1L cold water. Serve over ice in four glasses with a lemon slice each. Taste and add more syrup if needed.

s.note: Smooth chicken liver pâté with cognac, cornichons and baguette
s.how: Sear 400g trimmed chicken livers in butter until just pink. Flame with 2 tbsp cognac. Blitz with 150g soft butter, thyme and a sautéed shallot. Set in a dish under 50g melted butter for 4 hours. Serve with cornichons and warm baguette.

s.note: Cinnamon sugar cake doughnuts and coffee, eaten in the car
s.how: Warm 8 cake doughnuts in a 160C oven for 5 minutes. Toss in 100g caster sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water and pour into paper cups. Eat them hunched in front of the telly.

m.note: Seared sirloin with béarnaise and twice-fried frites
m.how: Reduce 60ml white wine vinegar with tarragon and a shallot to 2 tbsp. Whisk with 3 yolks over a low heat, then drizzle in 200g warm clarified butter. Fry 1kg potato chips twice. Sear 4 sirloins hard, rest 5 minutes and serve.

w.note: Silky baked custards turned out under amber caramel
w.how: Melt 150g sugar to an amber caramel and pour into 4 ramekins. Whisk 4 eggs, 2 yolks, 100g sugar, 500ml milk and the seeds of a vanilla bean. Pour over, bake in a water bath at 150C for 40 minutes, chill overnight and turn out.

d.note: Stewed black drip coffee in a chipped mug
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine and leave it on the hot plate for at least an hour. Pour into the oldest mugs you own, black, no sugar, and drink it like you're on a stakeout.

s.note: Devilled eggs with an olive slice eye staring up
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and halve. Mash the yolks with 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tsp Dijon and a pinch of cayenne. Pipe back into the whites and press a black olive slice on each so they stare up at you.

s.note: Smoky black bean dip with feta, coriander and corn chips
s.how: Blitz 2 drained tins black beans with 2 garlic cloves, juice of 2 limes, 1 tsp cumin and 1 chipotle in adobo until smooth. Spoon into a bowl and top with 80g crumbled feta and coriander. Serve with corn chips.

m.note: Cheeseburgers on black buns with pickles and burger sauce
m.how: Shape 800g beef mince into 4 patties and griddle to medium. Melt a slice of cheddar on each under a lid. Mix 100g mayo with chopped pickle and a little mustard for sauce. Serve on toasted charcoal buns with extra pickles.

w.note: Cake pops dipped in white chocolate and brushed silver
w.how: Crumble a 500g butter cake and mix with 100g cream cheese icing until it holds together. Roll into 16 balls, push in sticks and chill an hour. Dip in 300g melted white chocolate, set, then brush with silver lustre dust.

d.note: Very sweet homemade lemonade, the alien favourite
d.how: Make a syrup of 150g caster sugar dissolved in 150ml hot water and cool. Stir with the juice of 4 lemons and 1L cold water. Serve over ice in four glasses with a lemon slice each. Taste and add more syrup if needed.

s.note: Prawns sizzled in garlic butter with chilli, wine and lemon
s.how: Melt 80g butter until foaming. Add 6 sliced garlic cloves and a pinch of chilli flakes, then 600g peeled green prawns. Toss over high heat for 2 minutes, add a splash of white wine and lemon juice, and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

s.note: Crustless cucumber and egg sandwiches in neat fingers on a stand
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 10 minutes, cool, then mash with 2 tbsp mayo and chopped cress. Spread 150g cream cheese mixed with dill on bread and layer with thin cucumber. Use 12 slices white bread, cut off the crusts and cut into fingers.

m.n: The takeaway she passes off as home cooking
m.note: Real homemade shepherd's pie with buttery golden mash on top
m.how: Brown 750g lamb mince. Add 1 diced onion and 2 diced carrots, then 2 tbsp tomato paste, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and 250ml water. Simmer 40 minutes. Top with 1kg potatoes mashed with 60g butter and a splash of milk, then bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.note: Vanilla sponge under a cloud of mascarpone cream and strawberries
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Whip 250g mascarpone with 300ml cream and 2 tbsp sugar. Fill and cover the cake, then pile on 500g strawberries.

d.note: English breakfast tea brewed four minutes in a warmed pot
d.how: Warm the teapot with hot water and tip it out. Add 4 tea bags and 1L freshly boiled water, then brew 4 minutes. Pour into four cups with milk in first or after, as you like, and sugar on the side.

s.n: Prawn cocktail for the whole hotel
s.note: Iced prawns on crisp iceberg with Marie Rose and paprika
s.how: Poach 500g green prawns in salted water with lemon and a bay leaf for 2 minutes, then plunge into iced water and peel. Mix 4 tbsp mayo with 2 tbsp tomato sauce and a squeeze of lemon. Serve on shredded iceberg in glasses, dusted with paprika.

s.note: Warm blini with crème fraîche, salmon roe and chives
s.how: Warm 16 buckwheat blini on a tray at 180C for 5 minutes. Top each with a teaspoon of crème fraîche, about 150ml in total, then half a teaspoon of salmon roe and a few snipped chives. Serve straight away while they are still warm.

m.note: Eye fillet and grilled lobster tail with béarnaise
m.how: Reduce 60ml white wine vinegar with tarragon to 2 tbsp, whisk with 3 yolks over a low heat and drizzle in 200g warm clarified butter. Sear 4 eye fillet steaks to medium rare and rest. Split 2 lobster tails, brush with garlic butter and grill for 6 minutes.

w.note: Buttery shortbread cut like stamps, with a piped design
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g icing sugar, then mix in 250g plain flour and 60g rice flour. Roll to 6mm, cut into rectangles with a pinking cutter and bake at 160C for 20 minutes. Cool and pipe a little stamp design on each with icing.

d.note: The good brut bubbles, poured for every guest
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne in an ice bucket with water and ice for 30 minutes. Open with a gentle hiss, not a pop, and pour slowly into four flutes, topping up as the foam settles.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork and chive dumplings with vinegar and chilli oil
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with a chopped bunch of garlic chives, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp Shaoxing and 1 tsp sesame oil. Pleat into 30 gyoza wrappers. Fry until the bottoms crisp, add water and steam with the lid on for 4 minutes.

s.note: Crisp squid tossed with fried garlic, chilli and spring onion
s.how: Score 500g squid tubes and cut into strips. Toss in 100g potato starch with salt, white pepper and a pinch of five spice. Fry at 190C for 90 seconds. Wok-toss with fried garlic, 2 sliced chillies and spring onion.

m.note: Sticky charred five spice ribs, glazed in hoisin and honey
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with 4 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tsp five spice, 1 cube red fermented bean curd and 3 garlic cloves. Marinate overnight. Roast covered at 160C for 90 minutes, then uncover, glaze and blast at 220C until sticky.

w.note: Crisp vanilla fortune cookies, each with a paper fortune inside
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites with 100g sugar, then stir in 60g flour, 40g melted butter and a little vanilla. Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune while hot.

d.note: Cold plum wine over a big ice cube with soda
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of plum wine well. Put a large ice cube in each of four short glasses, pour about 120ml plum wine over each and top with a splash of soda water. Add a plum from the bottle if there are any.

s.note: Warm torn baguette with cultured butter and flaky salt
s.how: Warm 2 baguettes at 200C for 6 minutes until the crust crackles. Tear into chunks rather than slicing. Serve with 250g cultured butter left out of the fridge for an hour to soften, and a little dish of flaky salt for sprinkling.

s.note: Warm olives with orange peel and thyme, cornichons alongside
s.how: Warm 300g mixed olives gently in 3 tbsp olive oil with a few strips of orange peel, thyme sprigs and a crushed garlic clove for 5 minutes. Tip into a bowl and serve with cornichons and pickled onions in little dishes.

m.note: Spaghetti in slow-simmered tomato sauce with basil and parmesan
m.how: Gently cook 4 sliced garlic cloves in 4 tbsp olive oil. Add 2 tins San Marzano tomatoes crushed by hand and simmer 25 minutes. Cook 500g spaghetti, toss through the sauce with basil and 30g butter, and finish with grated parmesan.

w.note: Chocolate mousse under biscuit soil, with a mint sprig planted on top
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and cool slightly. Whisk in 3 yolks, then fold in 300ml whipped cream and 3 whites whipped to soft peaks. Layer in four small cups with 150g crushed chocolate biscuits as soil. Chill 3 hours and plant a mint sprig in each.

d.note: Ice-cold full cream milk in tall glasses
d.how: Chill 1L full cream milk in the coldest part of the fridge and put four tall glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Pour the milk to the brim. Stir a spoon of honey into any glass for anyone who wants it sweet.

s.note: Goat's cheese crostini with poached pear, honey and thyme
s.how: Slice a baguette thin on the bias, brush with oil and toast at 200C for 8 minutes. Poach 2 sliced pears in simmering water with honey for 5 minutes. Spread toasts with 150g whipped goat's cheese, top with pear and drizzle with honey and thyme.

s.note: Soft salted pretzels warmed through, with sharp grain mustard
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with 30g melted butter and sprinkle with coarse salt. Warm on a tray at 200C for 5 minutes until the crust is glossy. Serve warm on a board with a bowl of wholegrain mustard for dipping.

m.note: Whole roast snapper with fennel, beurre blanc and new potatoes
m.how: Score a 1.5kg snapper, stuff with lemon slices, sliced fennel and dill, then roast at 220C for 25 minutes. Boil 800g new potatoes. Reduce 1 shallot with 100ml white wine and 2 tbsp vinegar, then whisk in 150g cold butter cube by cube.

w.note: Dark chocolate mousse set in glasses
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 30g butter. Whisk in 4 yolks, then fold in 4 whites whipped to soft peaks with 40g sugar, then 150ml softly whipped cream. Spoon into four glasses and set in the fridge for 4 hours before serving.

d.note: Brut champagne in coupes, like it's 1876
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne to about 7C, around three hours in the fridge or 30 minutes in an ice bucket. Open gently and pour into four coupes, slowly, so the foam does not spill over the shallow rims.

s.note: Crisp rosemary lavash stacked with cheddar and apple like books
s.how: Cut 2 lavash breads into neat rectangles, brush with oil, sprinkle with chopped rosemary and bake at 180C for 8 minutes until crisp. Cool, then stack with slices of 200g vintage cheddar and thin apple slices like a little pile of books.

s.note: Light scones packed close, with jam and cream
s.how: Rub 60g cold butter into 350g self-raising flour, then mix in 250ml milk lightly with a knife. Pat out, cut into rounds and pack close on a tray. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with strawberry jam and 300ml whipped cream.

m.note: Tall stack of buttermilk pancakes with maple and warm blueberries
m.how: Whisk 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp sugar, 500ml buttermilk and 2 eggs. Rest 15 minutes. Cook ladlefuls in butter until bubbles set. Warm 250g blueberries in a pan for 3 minutes. Stack high with butter, maple syrup and the blueberries.

w.note: Rich dark chocolate cake under thick fudge frosting
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 200g butter. Whisk in 3 eggs, 250g sugar and 250ml buttermilk, then fold in 200g flour, 40g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Cover in frosting of 100g melted chocolate beaten with 100g butter and 150g icing sugar.

d.note: Iced water with lemon, cucumber and mint, nothing alive in it
d.how: Fill a big jug with plenty of ice. Add 1 sliced lemon, half a sliced cucumber and a handful of mint, then top with 1.5L cold water. Rest 10 minutes so the flavours come through, check carefully for newts, and pour.

s.note: Warm soft pretzels with butter, coarse salt and yellow mustard
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with 30g melted butter and sprinkle with coarse salt. Warm on a tray at 200C for 5 minutes until glossy. Cut in halves for sharing and serve with a squeeze bottle of yellow mustard.

s.note: Garlic-rubbed toasts with ripe tomato and basil
s.how: Grill 16 baguette slices until charred at the edges and rub each with a cut garlic clove. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes and dress with torn basil, salt and 2 tbsp good olive oil. Spoon on just before serving so the toasts stay crisp.

m.note: Rigatoni with sausage, fennel, white wine and cream
m.how: Brown 4 Italian sausages, skins off and crumbled. Add 1 sliced fennel bulb and 2 garlic cloves and cook 8 minutes. Deglaze with 125ml white wine, add 150ml cream, and toss with 500g cooked rigatoni and 60g grated parmesan.

w.note: Rustic hand-folded apple galette with cinnamon sugar
w.how: Roll a sheet of shortcrust pastry into a rough circle. Toss 4 sliced apples with 60g sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon and pile in the middle. Fold the edges up by hand, pleating as you go, and bake at 200C for 40 minutes until golden.

d.note: Pinot noir, slightly cool, in big glasses
d.how: Put a 750ml bottle of pinot noir in the fridge for 20 minutes to bring it to about 14C. Open it 20 minutes before pouring to let it breathe. Serve in big glasses, about 150ml each, with the rest for top-ups.

s.note: Buttery furikake popcorn, eaten with chopsticks
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pot with 3 kernels. When they pop, add 120g kernels, cover and shake until the popping slows. Toss with 50g melted butter, 3 tbsp furikake and a pinch of sugar. Hand out chopsticks and see who gives up first.

s.note: Crisp vegetable spring rolls with sweet chilli
s.how: Stir-fry 2 cups shredded cabbage, 1 grated carrot and 100g sliced shiitake. Add 50g soaked glass noodles, soy and white pepper, then cool. Roll tightly in 16 spring roll wrappers, sealing with water, and fry at 180C until golden. Serve with sweet chilli.

m.note: Double-fried chicken in a sweet, sticky chilli sauce with rice
m.how: Toss 800g diced chicken thighs in 100g potato starch and fry twice at 180C. Fry 8 dried chillies, 3 garlic cloves and ginger, then add 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp black vinegar, 3 tbsp sugar and 125ml stock. Toss the chicken through. Serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.note: Soft mochi wrapped around fresh mango and cream
w.how: Mix 150g glutinous rice flour, 50g sugar and 200ml coconut milk, then steam for 20 minutes, stirring halfway. Dust a board with cornflour and divide into 8. Wrap each around a cube of mango and a spoon of whipped cream. Chill 30 minutes.

d.note: Lightly sweet chrysanthemum tea, chilled over ice
d.how: Steep 15g dried chrysanthemum flowers in 1L just-boiled water with 50g rock sugar for 5 minutes. Strain, cool and chill well in the fridge. Pour over ice in four tall glasses and float a flower or two on top.

s.note: Chewy oat, date and peanut bars for the ride
s.how: Melt 100g butter, 80g honey and 80g brown sugar. Stir through 250g oats, 100g chopped dates, 80g peanuts and 40g mixed seeds. Press into a lined tin and bake at 170C for 25 minutes. Cool completely before cutting into bars.

s.note: Warm buttery salted pretzels with a squeeze of mustard
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with 30g melted butter and sprinkle with coarse salt. Warm on a tray at 200C for 5 minutes until glossy. Serve straight away with yellow mustard in a squeeze bottle for drawing lines across them.

m.note: Spiced chopped chicken over turmeric rice with white sauce
m.how: Marinate 800g chicken thighs in lemon, oregano, cumin and coriander for an hour. Griddle and chop. Cook 300g rice with 1 tsp turmeric. Mix 100g yoghurt, 100g mayo, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sugar and pepper. Serve on shredded lettuce with hot sauce.

w.note: Brown butter choc chip cookies with flaky salt
w.how: Brown 150g butter and cool. Beat with 200g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour, half a tsp bicarb and 200g choc chips. Rest overnight in the fridge. Roll into 16 balls, bake at 180C for 10 minutes and sprinkle with flaky salt.

d.note: Banana, berry, oat and peanut butter smoothie
d.how: Blend 2 bananas, 250g frozen berries, 40g rolled oats, 2 tbsp peanut butter and 800ml milk until completely smooth. Add a shot of espresso for anyone riding through traffic. Pour into four tall glasses and drink straight away.

s.note: Saltines, sharp cheddar, folded salami and pickled jalapeños
s.how: Cut 250g sharp cheddar into slabs and fold 150g sliced salami into quarters. Lay out on a chopping board with a sleeve of saltine crackers and a small bowl of pickled jalapeños. Eat it straight off the board on the couch.

s.note: Griddled franks with mustard and fried onions, wrapped in foil
s.how: Simmer 8 franks for 5 minutes, then griddle until blistered. Fry 2 sliced onions in oil until soft and golden. Steam 8 buns, fill with franks, onions and mustard, then wrap each in foil to keep warm until everyone is ready.

m.note: Slow-braised beef stew in red wine over buttery mash
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 1 onion, 2 carrots and 2 celery sticks, stir in 2 tbsp tomato paste, then add 250ml red wine, 500ml stock and thyme. Braise at 150C for 3 hours. Serve on 1kg potatoes mashed with butter.

w.note: Layered chocolate cake with buttercream and far too many candles
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 200ml milk. Bake in two tins at 170C for 35 minutes. Beat 200g butter, 300g icing sugar and 40g cocoa for buttercream. Fill, cover and add candles.

d.note: Cold lager in the bottle, drunk on the step
d.how: Chill eight 375ml bottles of lager in the fridge for at least three hours, or in a bucket of ice and water for 30 minutes. Hand them out with the caps already off and drink straight from the bottle.

s.note: Toasted buttered fruit loaf with a pot of strong tea
s.how: Toast 8 thick slices of fruit loaf until the edges crisp, butter generously and cut into fingers. Warm a teapot, add 4 tea bags and 1L boiling water and brew 4 minutes. Serve with milk on the side, like a guest in a burrow.

s.n: Bog of Eternal Stench garlic dip
s.note: Roasted garlic whipped into cream cheese, with crusty bread
s.how: Wrap 2 whole garlic heads in foil and roast at 180C for 45 minutes. Squeeze out the soft cloves and beat with 250g cream cheese, 100g sour cream, lemon juice and salt until smooth. Serve with torn baguette for dipping.

m.note: Slow-braised beef with mushrooms in red wine, mash on the side
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 1 onion, 2 carrots and 250g mushrooms, add 250ml red wine and 500ml stock, cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk and serve alongside.

w.note: Wine-poached peaches with mascarpone and crushed almond biscuits
w.how: Simmer 375ml white wine, 150g sugar and a split vanilla bean for 5 minutes. Add 4 halved peaches and poach 10 minutes, then slip off the skins and chill in the syrup. Serve with 250g mascarpone and crumbled almond biscuits.

d.note: Spiced apple and pear juice, warm or over ice
d.how: Pour 1L cloudy apple juice and 500ml pear juice into a pot with 2 cinnamon sticks and 3 star anise. Simmer gently for 10 minutes so the spices come through. Serve warm in mugs, or cool it and pour over ice.

s.note: Hand-chopped eye fillet with capers and shallot on toasted brioche
s.how: Finely chop 300g well-chilled eye fillet by hand. Mix with 1 diced shallot, 1 tbsp capers, 4 chopped cornichons, 1 tsp Dijon, a dash of Worcestershire and 1 yolk. Season well and serve with toasted brioche slices.

s.note: Iced prawns on crisp iceberg with Marie Rose and lemon
s.how: Poach 500g green prawns in salted water for 2 minutes, plunge into iced water and peel. Mix 4 tbsp mayo, 2 tbsp tomato sauce and a squeeze of lemon. Serve on shredded iceberg in glasses with a dusting of paprika and lemon wedges.

m.note: Butter-basted rib eye with a brandy peppercorn sauce
m.how: Dry-brine 4 rib eyes overnight. Sear hard, then baste with 60g butter and rosemary and rest 8 minutes. In the pan, crush 1 tbsp peppercorns, flame 60ml brandy, add 125ml stock and 200ml cream and reduce until it coats a spoon.

w.note: Baked New York cheesecake with a sour cream top
w.how: Mix 250g crushed biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 750g cream cheese with 200g sugar, 3 eggs and lemon zest. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 60 minutes. Spread 300g sour cream on top and bake 10 minutes more. Chill overnight.

d.note: Bourbon, sugar and bitters over a big cube, orange twist
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml bourbon, 10ml sugar syrup and 2 dashes aromatic bitters over ice for 30 seconds. Strain over one big ice cube in a short glass and twist a strip of orange peel over the top. Makes four.

s.note: Grilled garlic and chilli prawns with lemon myrtle butter
s.how: Toss 600g peeled king prawns with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 chopped chilli, lemon zest and 2 tbsp oil. Thread onto skewers and grill hot for 90 seconds a side. Brush with 50g butter melted with 1 tsp lemon myrtle and serve with lemon.

s.note: Little meat pies with puff lids and tomato sauce
s.how: Cook 500g beef mince with 1 onion, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp tomato sauce and 250ml stock, thicken and cool. Line patty tins with 2 sheets shortcrust, fill, top with 2 sheets puff and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

m.note: Crisp-skinned barramundi with lemon myrtle garlic butter
m.how: Score the skin of 4 barramundi fillets and pat very dry. Grill skin down over high heat until crisp, about 4 minutes, then flip for 1 minute. Melt 80g butter with 2 garlic cloves and 1 tsp lemon myrtle and spoon over.

w.note: Sponge squares in chocolate icing rolled in coconut
w.how: Cut a 500g butter sponge into 16 squares. Whisk 400g icing sugar, 40g cocoa, 20g melted butter and 150ml milk into a thin icing. Dip each square, drain and roll in 200g desiccated coconut. Set on a rack for an hour.

d.note: Aussie lager in cans, iced in an esky
d.how: Fill an esky with a bag of ice and some cold water so the cans sit in it. Bury 12 cans of lager for at least an hour. Hand them out in stubby holders, which are not optional.

s.note: Cucumber rounds topped with poached prawns and Marie Rose
s.how: Poach 300g green prawns for 2 minutes, chill and peel. Cut 2 cucumbers into thick rounds. Mix 3 tbsp mayo with 1 tbsp tomato sauce. Top each round with a prawn, a dot of sauce and a dill sprig and serve cold on a tray.

s.note: Cheddar, brie and blue with quince paste and grapes
s.how: Take 150g aged cheddar, 150g brie and 150g blue cheese out of the fridge an hour ahead. Arrange on a board with crackers, 100g quince paste cut into slices and a few small bunches of grapes.

m.note: Seared sirloin over cos with blue cheese and red wine dressing
m.how: Sear 2 large sirloins hard, rest and slice thin. Toss 2 heads cos with 250g halved cherry tomatoes and thin red onion. Whisk 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 6 tbsp oil and Dijon. Top with the steak and 100g crumbled blue cheese.

w.note: Tall vanilla cake slices with jam and meringue buttercream
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Whisk 3 whites with 150g sugar over hot water, then beat in 250g butter. Layer with raspberry jam and chill.

d.note: Brut champagne, chilled and poured into flutes
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne in an ice bucket with water and ice for 30 minutes. Open gently so it hisses rather than pops. Pour slowly into four flutes, letting the foam settle before topping up.

s.note: Tangy devilled eggs with paprika, best eaten sitting down
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and halve. Mash the yolks with 3 tbsp mayo, 1 tsp Dijon and a splash of pickle juice until smooth. Pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Serve chilled.

s.note: Thin biltong with dried peaches and salted macadamias
s.how: Roast 150g macadamias at 170C for 8 minutes and toss with salt while warm. Slice 250g biltong thinly across the grain. Pile on a board with 150g dried peaches and the macadamias in little bowls.

m.note: Grilled spiced sausage coil in rolls with tomato and onion relish
m.how: Simmer 2 sliced onions, 4 chopped tomatoes, 1 chilli and 1 tsp sugar for 20 minutes into a relish. Grill a 1kg coil of boerewors over coals or a hot grill for 15 minutes, turning once. Cut and serve in 4 long rolls with relish.

w.note: Bright vanilla cupcakes with pastel buttercream and sprinkles
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, tint in pastel colours, swirl on and add sprinkles.

d.note: Ice-cold American lager, opened on the back deck
d.how: Chill eight 355ml bottles of American lager in the fridge for at least three hours, or in a bucket of ice and water for 30 minutes. Crack them open on the back deck and drink straight from the bottle.

s.note: Egg and cress sandwiches cut into triangles
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Mash with 3 tbsp mayo, chopped chives and white pepper. Spread on 8 slices soft white bread, scatter with cress, close and cut into triangles. Serve straight away.

s.note: Twisted parmesan pastry straws that look like knitting
s.how: Brush 2 sheets puff pastry with beaten egg and cover one with 80g grated parmesan and a pinch of paprika. Lay the other on top, press, cut into strips and twist. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until golden and crisp.

m.note: Beef and ale pies with puff lids, no chicken anywhere
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, add 2 onions, thyme and 375ml ale and braise covered for 2.5 hours. Thicken, cool, then fill 4 pie tins lined with shortcrust. Top with puff, egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes.

w.note: Baked jam roly-poly with hot custard
w.how: Rub 100g butter into 250g self-raising flour, then add 150ml cold water to a soft dough. Roll to a rectangle, spread with 150g raspberry jam and roll up. Wrap loosely in baking paper and foil and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Serve with custard.

d.note: Strong breakfast tea in a big pot with milk and sugar
d.how: Warm a big teapot, add 5 tea bags and 1.2L boiling water and brew 5 minutes so it's properly strong. Pour into four mugs with milk and sugar on the side for everyone to sort out their own.

s.note: Thin golden fries, salted straight out of the oil
s.how: Cut 1kg russets into thin fries and soak in cold water for 30 minutes, then dry well. Fry at 140C for 5 minutes, rest, then fry at 190C until golden and crisp. Salt straight away and serve hot.

s.note: Thin rosewater sugar cookies with crushed rose petals
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 100g sugar and 1 tsp rose water, then mix in 200g flour. Roll thin, cut into rounds and press crushed dried rose petals on top. Bake at 170C for 9 minutes until just crisp at the edges.

m.note: Double smashed patties with special sauce on a three-piece bun
m.how: Mix 100g mayo, 2 tbsp relish, 1 tsp mustard, paprika and a dash of vinegar. Smash 8 thin patties from 800g mince, add cheese. Build each in a three-piece sesame bun with sauce, shredded iceberg, diced onion and pickles.

w.note: Flaky puff turnovers with buttery cinnamon apple
w.how: Cook 3 diced apples with 30g butter, 3 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon for 8 minutes, then cool. Cut 2 sheets puff pastry into quarters, fill, fold into triangles and crimp. Egg wash and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

d.note: Thick vanilla shakes blended with plenty of ice cream
d.how: For each shake, blend 3 scoops vanilla ice cream with 150ml cold milk until thick and smooth. Pour into a chilled tall glass and serve with a wide straw. Make four, one after the other, so they stay thick.

s.note: Warm damper with butter and golden syrup
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour and a pinch of salt. Mix in about 300ml milk to a soft dough, shape into a round and score a cross. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow. Serve warm with butter and golden syrup.

s.note: Thick sausages rolled in bread with onions and sauce
s.how: Grill 8 thick beef sausages slowly over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning often. Fry 2 sliced onions until soft and golden. Wrap each sausage in a slice of white bread with onions and a squeeze of tomato sauce.

m.note: Whole barra with lemon, ginger and coriander cooked in foil
m.how: Stuff a 1.5kg whole barramundi with lemon slices, a sliced knob of ginger and a bunch of coriander. Dot with 50g butter and wrap well in foil. Cook over hot coals or a hot grill for 20 minutes, turning once.

w.note: Crisp-shelled pavlova with cream, passionfruit and mango
w.how: Whip 4 whites to soft peaks, add 220g caster sugar gradually until glossy, then fold in 1 tsp cornflour and 1 tsp vinegar. Bake at 120C for 90 minutes and cool in the oven. Top with 300ml whipped cream, 4 passionfruit and a sliced mango.

d.note: Aussie lager in cans, straight from the esky
d.how: Fill an esky with a bag of ice and a little cold water. Bury 12 cans of lager for at least an hour before anyone sits down. Hand them out one at a time, cold enough to hurt your hand.

s.note: Hot-smoked salmon dip with dill and capers, bagel chips
s.how: Flake 200g hot-smoked salmon into 150g cream cheese and 100ml crème fraîche. Add lemon juice, chopped dill, 1 tbsp capers and 1 tsp horseradish. Slice 2 bagels thin, brush with oil and bake at 180C for 10 minutes into chips.

s.note: Brown butter popcorn with flaky salt
s.how: Cook 60g butter until it smells nutty and goes golden. Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil with 3 kernels, then add 120g kernels once they pop, cover and shake until popping slows. Toss with the brown butter and flaky salt.

m.note: Herb-crusted salmon with greens and lemon butter
m.how: Mix 50g panko with chopped parsley, lemon zest and oil. Press onto 4 salmon fillets and roast at 200C for 12 minutes. Steam 300g green beans. Melt 60g butter with lemon juice and spoon over everything.

w.note: Heart-shaped sugar cookies iced red and white
w.how: Brown 125g butter and cool. Beat with 100g sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour. Roll to 5mm, cut into hearts and bake at 180C for 9 minutes. Ice with 300g icing sugar mixed with egg white, half tinted red.

d.note: Slow pour-over coffee with milk on the side
d.how: Grind 60g medium roast beans. For each cup, pour 250ml water at 94C slowly over 15g grounds in a filter, in circles, over about three minutes. Serve with warm milk on the side for anyone who wants it.

s.note: Hot roasted peanuts with salt and cayenne
s.how: Spread 400g peanuts in the shell on a tray and roast at 180C for 20 minutes. Toss straight away with 1 tsp fine salt and a pinch of cayenne. Tip into a tin bucket and put an empty bowl out for the shells.

s.note: Warm torn sourdough with roasted garlic butter
s.how: Roast a garlic head wrapped in foil at 180C for 40 minutes. Squeeze into 125g soft salted butter and whip. Warm a sourdough round at 200C for 10 minutes, tear into chunks and serve with the butter.

m.note: Seafood stew of crab, clams, mussels and prawns in tomato
m.how: Soften 1 sliced fennel, 1 onion and 3 garlic cloves in oil. Add 1 tin tomatoes, 250ml white wine and 500ml fish stock, simmer 20 minutes. Add 1 crab, then 500g clams and mussels, then 300g prawns and 300g fish. Serve with sourdough.

w.note: One-bowl chocolate cake with thick fudge icing
w.how: Whisk 250g flour, 300g sugar, 60g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Add 125ml oil, 250ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 250ml hot coffee. Bake at 170C for 35 minutes. Ice with 250g icing sugar, 40g cocoa, 60g soft butter and a splash of hot water.

d.note: Ice-cold American lager in long neck bottles, straight from the fridge
d.how: Chill eight 355ml long necks of American lager in the fridge for at least three hours. Open them at the table and drink straight from the bottle, the way it's done in a bar like Torchy's.

s.note: Crisp ham croquetas with a creamy middle and lime
s.how: Melt 60g butter, stir in 80g flour, then whisk in 500ml milk until very thick. Add 200g chopped ham, chill overnight. Shape into logs, roll in 2 beaten eggs and 150g breadcrumbs, and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Serve with lime.

s.note: Grilled pineapple, mango and papaya with lime, honey and chilli salt
s.how: Cut half a pineapple, 2 mangoes and half a papaya into chunks and thread onto skewers. Grill hot for a minute a side. Brush with juice of 2 limes mixed with 2 tbsp honey and sprinkle with salt and chilli flakes.

m.note: Slow-roasted citrus pork, ham, Swiss and pickles, pressed and toasted
m.how: Marinate 1kg pork shoulder in juice of 2 oranges and 2 limes, garlic and oregano overnight. Roast at 160C for 4 hours and slice. Layer in 4 long rolls with 150g ham, Swiss, pickles and mustard. Press in a buttered pan until crisp.

w.note: Tangy lime custard on a biscuit crust with cream
w.how: Press 200g crushed biscuits mixed with 80g melted butter into a pie tin. Whisk a 395g tin condensed milk with 4 yolks, the zest of 2 limes and 125ml lime juice. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes, chill overnight and top with 300ml whipped cream.

d.note: Mint, lime and white rum over crushed ice with soda
d.how: For each drink, gently muddle 8 mint leaves with half a lime cut in wedges and 2 tsp sugar. Add 45ml white rum and fill with crushed ice. Top with soda water and stir from the bottom. Makes four.

s.note: Sticky honey mustard cocktail franks on toothpicks
s.how: Simmer 24 cocktail franks for 5 minutes and drain. Toss in a hot pan with 2 tbsp Dijon and 2 tbsp honey for 3 minutes until sticky and glazed. Spear each on a toothpick and serve while hot.

s.note: Little fish-shaped cheddar crackers, crisp and salty, for snacking
s.how: Pulse 150g grated cheddar, 60g cold butter and 100g flour with a pinch of salt until it forms a dough, adding a splash of water. Roll thin, cut into little fish shapes and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until crisp.

m.note: Griddled franks with mustard, onion, relish and sauerkraut
m.how: Simmer 8 franks for 5 minutes, then griddle until blistered. Warm 250g sauerkraut in a small pan. Steam 8 buns and fill with franks, mustard, chopped onion, sweet relish and the sauerkraut.

w.note: Cat-shaped shortbread iced orange with whiskers
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g icing sugar and mix in 350g flour. Roll to 6mm, cut into cat shapes and bake at 160C for 18 minutes. Ice with 200g icing sugar tinted orange and pipe on little whiskers in white.

d.note: Cold milk, or warm with honey and cinnamon
d.how: Pour 1L full cream milk into four glasses ice cold, or warm it gently in a pot with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of cinnamon until steaming. Don't boil it. Serve in mugs with a dusting of cinnamon on top.

s.note: Chicken and mushroom vol-au-vents with prosciutto asparagus
s.how: Bake 16 vol-au-vent cases until crisp. Fry 250g diced chicken thigh and 150g mushrooms, add 150ml cream and thyme and reduce. Fill the cases. Blanch 2 bunches asparagus and wrap each spear in half a slice of prosciutto.

s.note: Buttery salted popcorn in paper cones
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil with 3 kernels, and when they pop add 120g kernels, cover and shake until the popping slows. Toss with 50g melted butter and fine salt while hot. Roll paper into cones and fill them up.

m.note: Tarragon butter roast chicken with gravy, potatoes and peas
m.how: Dry-brine a 1.8kg chicken overnight. Push 60g butter mixed with chopped tarragon under the skin. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C until the thigh hits 72C, with 1kg potatoes. Make gravy with 250ml stock. Serve with buttered peas.

w.note: Hot fudge sundaes with cream, almonds and a cherry
w.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate with 150ml cream and 2 tbsp golden syrup into a hot fudge. Scoop vanilla ice cream into four tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream, toasted flaked almonds and a cherry.

d.note: Sweet lemonade turned pink with raspberry cordial
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Mix with the juice of 4 lemons, 1L cold water and 60ml raspberry cordial until pink. Serve over ice in four glasses with a lemon slice each.

s.note: Smoked salmon on buttered rye with lemon crème fraîche and dill
s.how: Butter 6 slices rye bread and cut into small squares. Top with 200g smoked salmon. Whip 100ml crème fraîche with lemon zest and put a dot on each, then add a dill sprig and cracked pepper. Serve cold.

s.note: Warm blini with crème fraîche, roe and chives
s.how: Warm 16 buckwheat blini on a tray at 180C for 5 minutes. Top each with a teaspoon of crème fraîche, about 150ml in all, half a teaspoon of salmon roe and a few snipped chives. Serve straight away on a silver tray if you have one.

m.note: Rare roast topside with Yorkshire puddings and gravy
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg topside at 200C until 52C inside, about an hour, and rest 20 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs, 150g flour and 300ml milk, pour into very hot oiled tins and bake at 220C for 20 minutes. Make gravy with 400ml stock and pan juices.

w.note: Vanilla custards under a torched sugar crust
w.how: Warm 600ml cream with a split vanilla bean. Whisk 6 yolks with 80g sugar and pour the cream over. Pour into 4 ramekins and bake in a water bath at 150C for 35 minutes. Chill overnight, then sprinkle with sugar and torch to amber.

d.note: Brut champagne in coupes, topped up before anyone asks
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne in an ice bucket for 30 minutes. Open gently and pour into four coupes slowly, so the foam stays in. Keep the bottle in the bucket and top glasses up before anyone has to ask.

s.note: Warm cake doughnuts shaken in cinnamon sugar
s.how: Warm 8 cake doughnuts on a tray at 160C for 2 minutes. Drop them into a paper bag with 100g caster sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon, fold the top and shake until coated. Eat them out of the bag.

s.note: Baked savoury mix of pretzels, peanuts and cereal
s.how: Toss 150g pretzels, 150g peanuts, 150g cereal squares and 50g sunflower seeds with 60g melted butter, 2 tbsp Worcestershire and 1 tsp garlic powder. Bake at 130C for 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes. Cool before bagging up.

m.note: Baked chicken enchiladas in red chilli sauce
m.how: Soak 4 dried chillies in hot water, blitz with 1 tin tomatoes and garlic and simmer 10 minutes. Poach and shred 600g chicken thighs. Roll in 8 corn tortillas, cover with sauce and 150g cheddar and bake at 190C for 20 minutes. Serve with sour cream.

w.note: Little yeasted doughnut balls rolled in cinnamon sugar
w.how: Mix 300g flour, 7g yeast, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 egg and 160ml warm milk into a soft dough and prove an hour. Roll into small balls and fry at 175C for 2 minutes. Roll in 100g caster sugar and 2 tsp cinnamon while warm.

d.note: Strong coffee with milk and sugar from a thermos
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water, strong. Warm 200ml milk and stir it in with sugar to taste. Pour into a thermos that's been warmed with hot water. Pour into the thermos lid cups one at a time.

s.note: Cheese balls rolled in toasted pecans, on toothpicks
s.how: Beat 250g cream cheese with 150g grated cheddar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 2 chopped spring onions. Roll into golf ball sizes and chill 30 minutes. Toast 100g pecans, crush and roll the balls in them. Spear each with a toothpick.

s.note: Fluffy buttermilk biscuits with butter and honey
s.how: Rub 100g cold butter into 300g flour with 3 tsp baking powder and salt. Stir in 250ml buttermilk, fold the dough over itself a few times and cut into rounds. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with butter and honey.

m.note: Glazed beef and pork meatloaf with mash and peas
m.how: Soak 80g breadcrumbs in 100ml milk. Mix lightly with 500g beef mince, 250g pork mince, 1 grated onion and 1 egg. Press into a loaf tin, glaze with 4 tbsp tomato sauce and 1 tbsp brown sugar and bake at 180C for an hour. Serve with mash and peas.

w.note: Double crust apple pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 1kg sliced Granny Smiths with 120g sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 2 tbsp flour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill, cover with 2 more sheets and egg wash. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes and rest an hour. Serve with vanilla ice cream.

d.note: Two jugs of cold lager for the table
d.how: Chill two big jugs in the freezer for 20 minutes. Fill each with 1.25L of very cold American lager, poured down the side so it doesn't foam over. Put them on the table with four glasses and let everyone help themselves.

s.note: Garlic-rubbed ciabatta with tomato, basil and red onion
s.how: Slice a ciabatta, grill until charred and rub with a cut garlic clove. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes and mix with torn basil, a little finely chopped red onion, 2 tbsp olive oil and salt. Spoon on just before serving.

s.note: Meatballs in tomato sugo with melted provolone on soft rolls
s.how: Roll 500g pork and veal mince with breadcrumbs, egg and parmesan into 12 balls. Brown, then simmer in 700ml passata for 25 minutes. Put each in a slider bun with a slice of provolone and basil and grill until the cheese melts.

m.note: Thin chicken in lemon, caper and butter sauce over angel hair
m.how: Pound 2 large chicken breasts thin, cut in half, flour and sear in oil. Add 125ml white wine, the juice of 2 lemons and 2 tbsp capers and reduce. Whisk in 60g butter. Toss with 400g cooked angel hair and serve the chicken on top.

w.note: Molten-centred chocolate puddings turned out warm
w.how: Melt 125g dark chocolate with 125g butter. Whisk 2 eggs and 2 yolks with 60g sugar until pale, combine and fold in 30g flour. Pour into 4 buttered moulds and bake at 200C for 10 minutes. Turn out and serve straight away.

d.note: Brut champagne in flutes, nothing else needed
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne to about 7C, three hours in the fridge or 30 minutes in an ice bucket. Open gently and pour into four flutes, slowly, so the foam settles before you top them up.

s.note: Crunchy baked caramel popcorn, like the stuff at the theme park
s.how: Pop 120g kernels. Boil 150g brown sugar, 80g butter and 3 tbsp golden syrup for 4 minutes, then stir in half a tsp bicarb. Pour over the popcorn, toss and bake at 120C for 45 minutes, stirring every 15. Cool and break up.

s.note: Cornmeal-battered franks fried on sticks, with mustard
s.how: Whisk 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 egg and 250ml buttermilk. Pat 8 franks dry and push onto sticks. Dip in batter and fry at 180C for 4 minutes until deep gold. Serve with mustard.

m.note: Brined smoky turkey drumsticks, roasted until falling apart
m.how: Dissolve 80g salt and 80g brown sugar in 2L water with 1 tbsp smoked paprika. Brine 4 turkey drumsticks overnight. Pat dry, rub with more paprika and roast at 150C for 2 hours until the meat pulls easily from the bone.

w.note: Glossy red toffee apples with fairy floss on the side
w.how: Push sticks into 4 apples. Boil 400g sugar, 125ml water and 1 tsp vinegar to 150C, then add a few drops of red colouring. Dip and twirl the apples, then set on baking paper. Serve with a bag of fairy floss.

d.note: Bright blue raspberry slushies that turn your tongue blue
d.how: Blitz 200ml blue raspberry cordial with 600ml cold water and 4 cups of ice in a blender until it is smooth and slushy. Pour into four cups and serve straight away with spoon straws before it melts.

s.note: Greek diner fries with oregano, lemon and feta
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into chips and fry twice, first at 140C, then at 185C. Toss while hot with 1 tsp dried oregano, the zest of a lemon, salt and 100g crumbled feta. Squeeze the lemon over just before serving.

s.note: Cheddar and Dijon toasties cut into soldiers
s.how: Spread 8 slices white bread with Dijon and fill with 200g sliced cheddar. Butter the outsides with 40g butter and griddle over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden and melted. Cut into soldiers.

m.note: Triple-decker turkey and bacon club with chips
m.how: Grill 8 rashers of bacon. Toast 12 slices bread. Layer 300g sliced turkey, bacon, lettuce and 2 sliced tomatoes with mayo across three slices for each sandwich. Pin with toothpicks and cut into triangles. Serve with potato chips.

w.note: Two-layer vanilla cake iced half pink, half green
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Beat 250g butter with 400g icing sugar, split and tint half pink and half green. Ice and pipe flowers.

d.note: Diner drip coffee with milk and sugar on the counter
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine and keep it on the hot plate. Pour into thick diner mugs and leave a jug of milk and the sugar on the counter so everyone fixes their own.

s.note: Cheese cubes, crackers, apple and tomatoes packed in lunch boxes
s.how: Cut 200g cheddar into small cubes. Slice 2 apples and toss in lemon juice so they don't brown. Pack each lunch box with cheese, a handful of crackers, apple slices and 250g cherry tomatoes shared between them.

s.note: Bright fruit cups with orange juice and mint
s.how: Dice 1 mango and a quarter of a pineapple, halve 250g strawberries and 200g grapes. Toss together with the juice of an orange. Spoon into four cups and top each with a mint leaf. Keep cold until serving.

m.note: Crumbed fish fingers with oven chips, tartare and peas
m.how: Cut 600g firm white fish into fingers. Dip in flour, 2 beaten eggs and 150g panko and shallow-fry for 2 minutes a side. Cut 1kg potatoes into chips, toss in oil and roast at 220C for 35 minutes. Serve with tartare and 300g peas.

w.note: Vanilla cupcakes in bright buttercream with sprinkles
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Beat 150g butter with 300g icing sugar, tint in primary colours, swirl on and add sprinkles.

d.note: Cold homemade chocolate milk, sweet and properly chocolatey
d.how: Whisk 3 tbsp cocoa and 3 tbsp sugar into 150ml hot milk until smooth with no lumps. Top up with 850ml cold milk, stir well and chill. Pour into four glasses and give it another stir before drinking.

s.note: Small bowls of sake rice, furikake, pickled plum and soft egg
s.how: Wash 300g short grain rice until the water runs clear. Cook with 360ml water and 2 tbsp sake. Boil 4 eggs for 6 and a half minutes, cool and peel. Serve rice in small bowls with furikake, a pickled plum and a halved egg.

s.note: Hot jalapeño cheese sauce with corn chips and jerky
s.how: Warm 375ml evaporated milk until steaming, then stir in 250g grated cheddar until smooth. Add 2 tbsp pickled jalapeño juice and a few chopped jalapeños. Pour into plastic bowls with corn chips and 100g beef jerky on the side.

m.note: Lard-simmered crispy pork in tortillas with charred tomatillo salsa
