m.how: Cut 1.2kg pork shoulder into big chunks and simmer slowly in 500g lard with 1 halved orange, 4 garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves and salt for 3 hours. Crisp in a hot pan. Char 400g tomatillos with a chilli, blitz with coriander. Serve in 16 warm tortillas.

w.note: Sponge soaked in three milks under whipped cream and cinnamon
w.how: Whisk 5 eggs with 200g sugar until thick, then fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake at 175C for 25 minutes. Prick all over and pour over 395g condensed milk, 375ml evaporated milk and 125ml milk. Soak overnight, then top with 300ml whipped cream and cinnamon.

d.note: Blanco tequila shots with lime and salt
d.how: Put four shot glasses and a bottle of blanco tequila in the freezer for an hour. Pour 30ml into each glass. Serve with a lime wedge and a pinch of flaky salt on the side, salt first, shot, then lime.

s.note: Griddled franks with mustard, relish and chopped onion
s.how: Simmer 8 franks in water for 5 minutes, then griddle until blistered all over. Steam 8 hot dog buns until soft. Fill with franks and top with yellow mustard, sweet relish and a spoon of finely chopped onion.

s.note: Garlic parmesan popcorn piled high in a big bowl
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a big pot with 3 kernels. When they pop, add 120g kernels, cover and shake until popping slows. Toss with 50g melted butter, 1 tsp garlic powder and 40g finely grated parmesan while still hot.

m.note: Creamy chicken stew with fluffy dumplings steamed on top
m.how: Simmer 800g chicken thighs with 1 onion, 2 celery sticks, 2 carrots, thyme and 1.5L stock for 40 minutes. Shred the chicken back in. Mix 200g self-raising flour, 50g butter and 150ml milk, drop spoonfuls on top and steam covered for 15 minutes.

w.note: Lemon drizzle loaf soaked in lemon syrup while hot
w.how: Beat 175g butter with 175g sugar, add 3 eggs, then fold in 175g self-raising flour and the zest of 2 lemons. Bake at 170C for 50 minutes. Mix the juice of 2 lemons with 100g sugar and pour over the hot loaf.

d.note: Eight lagers in a bucket of ice, one for every day
d.how: Fill a bucket with a bag of ice and some cold water. Bury eight 355ml bottles of American lager for 30 minutes until icy. Crack them open and toast to how close everyone is to retirement.

s.note: Baked corn chips with beans, cheddar and jalapeños, salsa on top
s.how: Layer a 300g bag of corn chips in a tray with a drained tin of black beans, 200g grated cheddar and sliced jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes. Top with sour cream and 2 diced tomatoes tossed with onion, lime and salt.

s.note: Homemade beef jerky dried low and slow
s.how: Slice 500g partly frozen beef topside very thin. Marinate overnight in 60ml soy, 2 tbsp Worcestershire, 2 tbsp brown sugar and lots of pepper. Pat dry, lay on racks and dry at 70C for 4 hours. Cool and store in a bag.

m.note: Creamy clam chowder in toasted sourdough bowls
m.how: Fry 150g diced bacon, add 1 onion and 2 celery sticks. Add 500g diced potatoes and 500ml water, simmer 15 minutes. Add 1kg clams, cover until they open, then 250ml cream and thyme. Ladle into 4 hollowed, toasted sourdough rounds.

w.note: Sticky golden syrup pecan pie on a crisp buttery crust
w.how: Blind-bake a pie tin lined with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust. Whisk 3 eggs, 250ml golden syrup, 100g brown sugar and 60g melted butter. Stir in 200g pecans, pour in and bake at 170C for 45 minutes until just set. Cool before slicing.

d.note: Ice-cold lager, cold enough to fog the glass
d.how: Chill eight 355ml bottles of American lager for at least three hours and put four glasses in the freezer for 20 minutes. Pour each beer down the side of a frosted glass so the head stays small.

s.note: Little wedges of Swiss, cheddar and gouda with fruit
s.how: Take 150g Swiss, 150g cheddar and 150g gouda out of the fridge an hour ahead. Cut into small wedges and poke holes in the Swiss with a skewer. Arrange with crackers, a bunch of grapes and a fanned apple.

s.note: Golden yeasted buns filled with beef, onion and dill
s.how: Mix 400g flour, 7g yeast, 250ml warm milk, 1 tsp sugar and 30g butter into a soft dough and prove an hour. Fry 400g beef mince with 1 onion and dill, then cool. Fill 12 rounds of dough, seal and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

m.note: Beetroot and cabbage soup with dill and sour cream
m.how: Grate 3 beetroots and 2 carrots and shred a quarter cabbage. Simmer with 2 diced potatoes in 1.5L beef stock for 40 minutes. Add 2 tbsp vinegar and plenty of dill. Serve with a big spoon of sour cream and rye bread.

w.note: Dark spiced honey cake made with coffee
w.how: Whisk 250g honey, 125ml oil, 3 eggs, 150g brown sugar and 125ml strong coffee. Fold in 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder and 2 tsp mixed spice. Pour into a lined tin and bake at 170C for 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.

d.note: Rich hot cocoa with a pinch of salt
d.how: Whisk 4 tbsp cocoa and 4 tbsp sugar with a splash of milk into a smooth paste. Add 1L milk and a pinch of salt and heat, whisking, until steaming but not boiling. Pour into four mugs.

s.note: Baked nachos with cheddar, jalapeños and black beans
s.how: Spread a 300g bag of corn chips on a tray. Scatter over a drained tin of black beans, 200g grated cheddar and sliced jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes until melted. Top with sour cream and a jar of salsa.

s.note: Smoky buttered pretzels and peanuts, baked and bagged for the ride
s.how: Toss 200g hard pretzels and 200g roasted peanuts with 50g melted butter and 1 tsp smoked paprika. Spread on a tray and bake at 160C for 15 minutes, stirring once. Cool and tip into paper bags.

m.note: Chargrilled citrus skirt steak in doubled corn tortillas
m.how: Marinate 800g skirt steak in the juice of 2 limes and 1 orange, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp cumin for 2 hours. Grill very hot for 3 minutes a side, rest and chop. Serve in doubled corn tortillas with onion, coriander and salsa verde.

w.note: Choc chip cookie ice cream sandwiches rolled in sprinkles
w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream for 5 minutes. Sandwich a thick scoop between two soft choc chip cookies, using 8 cookies for 4 sandwiches. Roll the edges in sprinkles, wrap in baking paper and freeze for an hour.

d.note: Cold brew over ice with milk and a scoop of ice cream
d.how: Steep 100g coarsely ground coffee in 1L cold water in the fridge overnight, then strain. Pour over ice in four tall glasses, about 200ml each, add a splash of milk and float a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top.

s.note: Pink beetroot-pickled eggs from a saloon jar
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Heat 250ml white vinegar, 125ml beetroot juice from a tin, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp mustard seeds and 1 tsp peppercorns. Pour over the eggs in a jar and refrigerate 3 days until pink.

s.note: Cast iron cornbread with honey butter
s.how: Heat a buttered cast iron pan in a 220C oven. Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 250ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter briefly. Pour into the hot pan and bake 20 minutes. Serve with 60g butter beaten with 2 tbsp honey.

m.note: Texas-style beef chilli, no beans, with cornbread
m.how: Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 1 onion and 4 garlic cloves, add 4 soaked and blitzed dried chillies, 2 tsp cumin and 1 tin crushed tomatoes. Braise covered for 3 hours until tender. Serve with the cornbread.

w.note: Lattice-topped peach pie, served warm with a jug of cream
w.how: Toss 6 sliced peaches with 100g sugar, the juice of a lemon and 2 tbsp cornflour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice from 2 more sheets. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes and serve with 300ml cream.

d.note: Rye whiskey neat with a jug of water
d.how: Pour 45ml rye whiskey neat into each of four small glasses. Put a jug of cool water on the table so everyone can add a few drops to open it up. Sip slowly, the way Doc would.

s.note: Warm chilli honey peanuts in little paper bags
s.how: Toss 300g honey-roasted peanuts with half a tsp chilli flakes and a pinch of smoked salt. Warm on a tray at 160C for 5 minutes, then cool for a few minutes. Divide between four small paper bags.

s.note: Prawn cocktail in martini glasses with spicy cocktail sauce
s.how: Poach 500g green prawns for 2 minutes, plunge into iced water and peel. Mix 100ml tomato sauce with 1 tbsp horseradish, lemon juice and a dash of hot sauce. Serve on shredded iceberg in martini glasses with lemon wedges.

m.note: Garlic butter sirloin with a loaded baked potato
m.how: Bake 4 large potatoes at 200C for an hour. Sear 4 sirloins hard and rest 5 minutes. Mash 60g butter with 2 garlic cloves and put a slice on each steak. Split the potatoes and load with sour cream and chives.

w.note: Vanilla cake shaped like a bunny, covered in coconut
w.how: Cut a round sponge cake into a body and two ears. Beat 200g butter with 350g icing sugar and cover the cake. Press 100g shredded coconut all over. Tint a little coconut pink for the ears and put it in a box with a bow.

d.note: Bourbon neat in a tumbler with water on the side
d.how: Pour 45ml bourbon neat into each of four heavy tumblers. Put a jug of cool water on the table for anyone who wants a few drops. Sip it slowly while the rest of the cons argue.

s.note: Herring in dill sour cream on buttered dark rye
s.how: Drain 300g pickled herring and cut into bite pieces. Mix with 150g sour cream, chopped dill and half a thinly sliced red onion. Butter 6 slices dark rye, cut into squares and spoon the herring on top.

s.note: All-beef franks with the full Chicago set of toppings
s.how: Simmer 8 all-beef franks for 5 minutes. Steam 8 poppy seed buns. Fill and top each with yellow mustard, sweet relish, chopped onion, tomato wedges, a pickle spear, pickled peppers and a pinch of celery salt.

m.note: Seared beef strips in a mushroom, mustard and sour cream sauce
m.how: Sear 600g eye fillet strips fast in batches and set aside. Brown 300g mushrooms and 1 onion, add 1 tsp paprika, 1 tbsp Dijon and 250ml stock and reduce. Stir in 200g sour cream off the heat, add the beef back. Serve over 400g egg noodles.

w.note: Thin honey cake layers stacked with sour cream frosting
w.how: Melt 100g honey, 100g butter and 150g sugar, whisk in 3 eggs and 1 tsp bicarb, then 450g flour. Roll into 8 thin discs and bake each 6 minutes at 180C. Layer with 600g sour cream beaten with 395g condensed milk. Coat in crumbs and rest overnight.

d.note: Freezer-cold vodka with rye bread and a pickle
d.how: Keep a bottle of vodka in the freezer overnight with four small glasses. Pour 30ml into each glass. Follow each shot with a bite of rye bread and a pickle, Russian style.

s.note: Warm salted pretzels with a beer cheese dip
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with butter, sprinkle with salt and warm at 200C for 5 minutes. Melt 150g cheddar into 125g cream cheese and 100ml lager in a small pot, stirring until smooth. Serve the dip warm with the pretzels.

s.note: Crisp potato skins filled with cheddar, bacon and sour cream
s.how: Bake 8 small potatoes at 200C for 45 minutes. Halve, scoop out most of the flesh and brush with 40g butter. Crisp at 220C for 10 minutes, fill with 150g cheddar and 150g cooked bacon and bake 5 more minutes. Top with sour cream and chives.

m.note: Chuck and mince chilli with kidney beans, sour cream and cheese
m.how: Brown 600g diced beef chuck and 400g mince. Add 1 onion, 2 tbsp chilli powder and 1 tsp cumin, then 2 tins tomatoes. Braise 2.5 hours, adding 2 tins kidney beans for the last 30 minutes. Serve with sour cream and grated cheddar.

w.note: Gingerbread planes and snowflakes, iced white
w.how: Melt 125g butter, 100g brown sugar and 100g golden syrup. Stir in 300g flour, 2 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon and half a tsp bicarb. Chill an hour, roll and cut into planes and snowflakes. Bake at 180C for 10 minutes and ice with 200g icing sugar.

d.note: Cold American lager in a pint glass
d.how: Chill 2L of American lager in bottles or cans for at least three hours. Pour into four pint glasses, tilted at first, then straight to build a small head, like the bar at the airport.

s.note: Brown butter popcorn in striped paper bags
s.how: Cook 60g butter until golden and nutty. Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil with 3 kernels, then add 120g kernels once they pop, cover and shake until the popping slows. Toss with the brown butter and flaky salt and fill striped paper bags.

s.note: Blistered franks with mustard and sauce, wrapped in foil
s.how: Simmer 8 franks for 5 minutes, then griddle until blistered. Steam 8 buns, fill with the franks and squeeze over yellow mustard and tomato sauce. Wrap each tightly in foil like a cinema candy bar would.

m.note: Thick rib eye with garlic butter and a loaded baked potato
m.how: Dry-brine 2 thick rib eyes overnight. Bake 4 potatoes at 200C for an hour. Sear the steaks, finish at 200C to 54C inside and rest. Top with 60g garlic butter, slice to share and load the potatoes with sour cream and 150g crispy bacon.

w.note: Hot fudge sundaes with salted peanuts and a cherry
w.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate with 150ml cream and 2 tbsp golden syrup. Scoop vanilla ice cream into four bowls, pour over the hot fudge and top with whipped cream, a handful of salted peanuts and a cherry.

d.note: Cold chocolate milk made from scratch
d.how: Whisk 3 tbsp cocoa and 3 tbsp sugar into 150ml hot milk until smooth. Top up with 850ml cold milk and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes. Stir again and pour into four glasses.

s.note: Yeasted buckwheat blini with sour cream, smoked salmon and dill
s.how: Mix 100g buckwheat flour, 100g plain flour, 7g yeast and 300ml warm milk and rest an hour. Cook small spoonfuls in butter until golden. Top each with sour cream, a curl of smoked salmon and dill.

s.note: Homemade sour dill pickles with buttered rye
s.how: Pack 1kg small cucumbers into a jar with 4 garlic cloves, dill and 1 tsp peppercorns. Pour over a cooled brine of 1L water and 50g salt. Leave on the bench for 4 days until sour. Serve with buttered rye bread.

m.note: Little beef and pork dumplings tossed in butter, dill and sour cream
m.how: Mix 300g flour, 1 egg and 125ml water into a firm dough and rest. Mix 250g beef mince, 250g pork mince and 1 grated onion. Roll the dough thin, cut rounds, fill and seal. Boil 5 minutes, toss in 50g butter and dill, serve with sour cream.

w.note: Layered honey cake with sour cream frosting, rested overnight
w.how: Melt 100g honey, 100g butter and 150g sugar, whisk in 3 eggs and 1 tsp bicarb, then 450g flour. Roll into 8 thin discs and bake each 6 minutes at 180C. Layer with 600g sour cream beaten with 395g condensed milk and coat in crumbs.

d.note: Freezer vodka in chilled glasses, pickle on the side
d.how: Keep a bottle of vodka and four small glasses in the freezer overnight. Pour 30ml into each glass and drink in one go, then chase it with a bite of dill pickle. One round is plenty before the fight.

s.note: Soft milk rolls brushed with butter and flaky salt
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 300ml warm milk, 50g butter, 2 tbsp sugar and 1 egg into a soft dough. Prove an hour, shape 12 rolls and prove 30 minutes more. Bake at 190C for 18 minutes and brush with butter and flaky salt.

s.note: Little squares of sponge with jam and cream
s.how: Cut a sponge cake into 16 small squares and split each in half. Whip 300ml cream to soft peaks. Fill each with a little raspberry jam and cream, put the tops back on and dust with icing sugar.

m.note: Saffron fish stew with rouille and toasted baguette
m.how: Soften 1 fennel, 1 leek, 1 onion and 3 garlic cloves in oil with saffron, orange peel and 1 tin tomatoes. Add 1L fish stock and simmer 20 minutes. Add 500g fish, then 500g mussels and 300g prawns. Serve with rouille and toasted baguette.

w.note: Vanilla layer cake piped Happy Birthday Captain in blue
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 200g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 25 minutes. Beat 250g butter with 400g icing sugar, fill and cover the cake, then pipe the message in blue.

d.note: Strong black drip coffee in steel mugs
d.how: Brew 70g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine so it comes out strong. Pour black into steel mugs, no milk, no sugar, and keep the pot going all night like a ship's galley.

s.note: Caramelised onion dip with ridged chips
s.how: Cook 2 sliced onions slowly in oil for 40 minutes until deep brown, then cool and chop. Stir into 250g sour cream and 125g cream cheese with a crushed garlic clove, salt and chopped chives. Serve with ridged potato chips.

s.note: Parmesan crackers cut into little bone shapes
s.how: Rub 80g cold butter into 150g flour, then mix in 60g grated parmesan and 1 egg into a dough. Roll to 4mm, cut into bone shapes and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack.

m.n: Steak, and the bone for Hooch
m.note: T-bones with garlic butter, roast potatoes and beans
m.how: Roast 1kg halved potatoes at 220C for 45 minutes. Sear 4 T-bones hard, finish at 200C for 6 minutes and rest. Top with 60g butter mashed with 2 garlic cloves. Steam 300g green beans. Save a bone for the dog.

w.note: Vanilla ice cream with cream, shortbread and salted caramel
w.how: Cook 100g sugar to amber, whisk in 100ml cream and a pinch of salt, and cool. Scoop vanilla ice cream into four cups, top with 200ml whipped cream, crushed shortbread and a drizzle of the caramel.

d.note: Strong black tea, chilled, with lemon and mint
d.how: Steep 6 black tea bags in 1L just-boiled water for 5 minutes, remove and stir in 60g sugar while hot. Chill completely. Pour over ice in four tall glasses with lemon slices and a sprig of mint.

s.note: Steamed pork and prawn siu mai with a carrot dot
s.how: Mix 300g pork mince, 150g chopped prawns, 3 chopped shiitake, 1 tbsp grated ginger and 1 tbsp soy. Spoon into 24 wonton wrappers, pinch up the sides leaving the top open and add a dot of grated carrot. Steam for 8 minutes.

s.note: Puffed five spice wonton crisps with sweet chilli
s.how: Cut 20 wonton wrappers into triangles. Fry at 180C in batches for about 30 seconds until puffed and golden. Drain and toss with salt and a pinch of five spice. Serve with sweet chilli sauce for dipping.

m.note: Five spice roast duck with pancakes, cucumber and hoisin
m.how: Prick a 2kg duck all over and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight. Rub inside with five spice and salt. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes, glazing with 2 tbsp honey and 2 tbsp soy for the last 15. Serve with 20 pancakes, cucumber, spring onion and hoisin.

w.note: Crisp vanilla fortune cookies with a paper fortune inside
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites with 100g sugar, then stir in 60g flour, 40g melted butter and a little vanilla. Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune.

d.note: Cold lager straight from an esky on deck
d.how: Fill an esky with a bag of ice and a little water. Bury eight 375ml bottles of lager for an hour. Hand them out on the back deck and drink them straight from the bottle.

s.note: Neat rows of cheese, crackers, grapes and cocktail onions
s.how: Cut 200g cheddar into cubes. Thread cubes onto toothpicks with a green grape and a cocktail onion. Lay them out in neat rows on a tray beside a row of crackers, like an old airline snack service.

s.note: Warm salted nuts in little packets
s.how: Mix 200g dry-roasted peanuts and 100g almonds with a pinch of sugar and salt. Warm on a tray at 160C for 5 minutes. Cool slightly and divide into small paper packets, one for each passenger.

m.note: Peppercorn sirloin with mash and beans on a tray
m.how: Sear 4 sirloins hard and rest. Crush 1 tbsp peppercorns into the pan, add 250ml cream and reduce until thick. Mash 1kg potatoes with butter and milk. Steam 300g green beans. Serve on trays, airline style.

w.note: Baked cheesecake slab in neat squares with a cherry
w.how: Mix 250g crushed biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a slab tin. Beat 750g cream cheese, 200g sugar, 3 eggs and 150g sour cream. Bake in a water bath at 150C for 50 minutes. Chill overnight, cut into squares and top each with a cherry.

d.note: Drip coffee poured black, straight from the pot
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine. Carry the pot around and pour into each cup black. Offer refills constantly, whether or not anyone has asked, and try not to spill it.

s.note: Crisp hot honey wings with blue cheese dip
s.how: Dry 1kg chicken wings in the fridge overnight. Bake at 220C for 45 minutes until crisp. Melt 60g butter with 80ml hot sauce and 1 tbsp honey and toss. Mix 80g blue cheese into 150g sour cream to dip. Serve with celery sticks.

s.note: Bacon-wrapped jalapeños filled with cream cheese
s.how: Halve and seed 12 jalapeños. Mix 150g cream cheese with 60g grated cheddar and fill each half. Wrap in half a rasher of bacon, 12 rashers in total, and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until the bacon is crisp.

m.note: Slow-cooked peppery brisket with pickles and white bread
m.how: Rub a 2kg brisket with 2 tbsp salt, 2 tbsp cracked pepper and 1 tbsp smoked paprika. Wrap and cook at 140C for 8 hours until it wobbles. Rest an hour and slice thick. Serve with white bread, pickles and barbecue sauce.

w.note: Chocolate sheet cake with fudge frosting and sprinkles
w.how: Beat 200g butter with 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 200ml milk. Bake in a tray at 175C for 30 minutes. Beat 150g butter, 300g icing sugar and 40g cocoa, spread on and cover with sprinkles.

d.note: Cold lager poured into red plastic cups
d.how: Chill 3L of American lager in bottles in a big tub of ice for an hour. Pour into red plastic cups and pass them around. Grown-ups only, and someone has to stay sensible.

s.note: Stuffed mushrooms with cream cheese, garlic and parmesan
s.how: Remove the stems from 20 button mushrooms. Mix 150g cream cheese with 2 crushed garlic cloves, 40g parmesan and 30g breadcrumbs. Fill the caps, scatter more crumbs on top and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden.

s.note: Warm glazed doughnuts and a pot of plain drip coffee
s.how: Warm 8 glazed doughnuts on a tray at 160C for 2 minutes until the glaze turns glossy again. Serve on a plain plate with paper napkins and a pot of drip coffee made from 60g grounds and 1L water.

m.note: Braised beef chuck with carrots and potatoes
m.how: Brown a 1.5kg chuck roast all over. Add 2 sliced onions, 4 carrots and 500ml stock, cover and braise at 160C for 3 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes for the last hour. Thicken the juices into gravy and serve.

w.note: Double crust apple pie with cinnamon
w.how: Toss 1kg sliced Granny Smiths with 120g sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and 2 tbsp flour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill and cover with 2 more. Egg wash and bake at 190C for 50 minutes. Rest an hour before slicing.

d.note: Plain black drip coffee, refilled without comment
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine. Pour black into plain mugs. When a cup gets low, refill it without saying anything. Just the coffee, nothing else.

s.note: Garlic, chilli and lime prawns grilled on skewers
s.how: Toss 600g peeled king prawns with 3 crushed garlic cloves, 1 chopped chilli, the zest and juice of a lime and 2 tbsp oil. Thread onto skewers and grill over hot coals for 90 seconds a side. Serve with lime wedges.

s.note: Baked nachos with pico de gallo and guacamole
s.how: Layer 300g corn chips with a drained tin of black beans, 200g cheddar and jalapeños and bake at 200C for 8 minutes. Mash 2 avocados with lime and salt. Dice 2 tomatoes with onion and coriander. Spoon both on top.

m.note: Beer-battered fish tacos with cabbage and chipotle crema
m.how: Whisk 150g flour with 250ml cold lager. Dip 500g flathead strips and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Mix 150g sour cream with 1 chipotle and lime juice. Serve in 12 warm tortillas with shredded cabbage, diced tomato and onion, and the crema.

w.note: Classic banana split with fudge, strawberries, cream and nuts
w.how: Split 4 bananas lengthways into four dishes. Add a scoop each of vanilla, chocolate and strawberry ice cream. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream for fudge. Top with fudge, sliced strawberries, whipped cream, chopped nuts and a cherry.

d.note: Mexican lager with lime, from a cooler in the sand
d.how: Bury eight 355ml bottles of Mexican lager in a cooler full of ice for an hour. Push a wedge of lime into the neck of each bottle just before handing it over. Drink it by the fire.

s.note: Crisp vegetables on ice with green goddess dressing
s.how: Blitz 100g mayo, 100g sour cream, a handful of parsley, a few tarragon leaves, chives, 2 anchovies and lemon juice until green and smooth. Arrange baby carrots, radishes, cucumber and sugar snaps on ice around the bowl.

s.note: Mini franks in buns with loose beef chilli, mustard and onion
s.how: Brown 250g beef mince with 1 finely chopped onion, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp cumin, then add 125ml water and simmer 15 minutes until loose. Simmer 16 cocktail franks. Put each in a mini bun with chilli, mustard and raw onion.

m.note: Rib eye and corn over coals with chimichurri and potato salad
m.how: Blitz parsley, 1 tsp oregano, 3 garlic cloves, a chilli, 60ml red wine vinegar and 125ml oil for chimichurri. Boil 1kg potatoes and dress with mayo and spring onion. Grill 4 rib eyes and 4 corn cobs over hot coals and serve together.

w.note: Banana split with three ice creams, hot fudge and cream
w.how: Split 4 bananas lengthways into four long dishes. Add a scoop each of vanilla, chocolate and strawberry ice cream. Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream and pour over. Top with whipped cream, chopped nuts and a cherry.

d.note: Ice-cold lager, one in a glass and one from the can
d.how: Chill eight 375ml cans of American lager for at least three hours. Pour half of them into chilled glasses for the Rosewoods at the table and hand the rest out in the can for the Taggarts.

s.note: Warm sourdough with salted butter and oil with dukkah
s.how: Warm a sourdough loaf at 200C for 8 minutes and tear into chunks. Serve with 125g soft salted butter and a shallow dish of extra virgin olive oil with 3 tbsp dukkah scattered on top for dipping.

s.note: Garlic chilli prawns in butter and white wine, with bread
s.how: Heat 3 tbsp olive oil, add 5 sliced garlic cloves and 1 sliced chilli, then 600g peeled green prawns. Toss over high heat for 2 minutes. Add 60g butter, a splash of white wine and parsley. Serve with bread for the juices.

m.note: Butter-basted rib eye with béarnaise and frites
m.how: Reduce 60ml white wine vinegar with tarragon to 2 tbsp, whisk with 3 yolks over low heat and drizzle in 200g warm clarified butter. Fry 1kg potato chips twice. Sear 4 rib eyes, baste with 40g butter, thyme and garlic, rest and serve.

w.note: Fudgy walnut chocolate squares with flaky salt
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour and 100g toasted walnuts. Bake in a lined tin at 175C for 25 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky salt, cool and cut into squares.

d.note: Single malt Scotch neat, with a few drops of water
d.how: Pour 30ml single malt Scotch into each of four small tumblers. Add a few drops of water with a teaspoon to open it up. Sip slowly, the way a retired SAS man would after a long day.

s.note: Iced prawns piled on crushed ice with a horseradish cocktail sauce
s.how: Poach 600g green prawns in salted water for 2 minutes, plunge into iced water and peel, leaving the tails on. Mix 125ml tomato sauce with 1 tbsp horseradish and lemon juice. Pile the prawns on a bag of crushed ice with the sauce and lemon wedges.

s.note: Crisp golden hash browns, each with a fried egg on top
s.how: Grate 800g potatoes, squeeze out as much liquid as you can and season well. Press into 8 thin cakes and fry in 40g butter and a little oil for 5 minutes a side until deep golden. Top each with a fried egg and chives.

m.note: Toasted burritos of soft eggs, chorizo, potato, cheddar and salsa
m.how: Dice and fry 300g potatoes until crisp, then add 200g diced chorizo. Softly scramble 8 eggs. Fill 4 large flour tortillas with the eggs, potato, chorizo, 100g cheddar and a fresh salsa of 2 tomatoes and onion. Roll and toast in a dry pan.

w.note: Lemon butter cake filled with lemon curd and vanilla buttercream
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 200g self-raising flour and lemon zest. Bake in two tins at 170C for 25 minutes. Fill with lemon curd and cover with 250g butter beaten with 400g icing sugar. Chill before slicing.

d.note: Chilled herbal liqueur shots, or a cold lager for the sensible
d.how: Put a bottle of herbal liqueur and four shot glasses in the freezer for an hour. Pour 30ml into each glass and toast on the roof. Keep a few cold lagers in the fridge for anyone who would rather remember the night.

s.note: Charred corn rolled in butter, salt and smoked paprika
s.how: Boil 4 corn cobs in salted water for 5 minutes, then char on a hot grill for about 6 minutes, turning. Roll each in melted butter, about 60g in total, and sprinkle with flaky salt and smoked paprika.

s.note: Crisp apple slices with honey cinnamon yoghurt to dip
s.how: Slice 3 crisp apples and toss in the juice of a lemon so they don't brown. Whip 250g Greek yoghurt with 2 tbsp honey and half a tsp cinnamon. Fan the apples around a bowl of the yoghurt for dipping.

m.note: Beef braised in dark ale with onion and carrot
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Soften 2 onions and 3 carrots in the same pot. Add 375ml dark ale and 500ml stock, cover and braise at 150C for 3 hours until the beef falls apart. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: Double crust apple pie with cinnamon and nutmeg
w.how: Toss 1kg sliced Granny Smiths with 120g sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon, a grating of nutmeg and 2 tbsp flour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill and cover with 2 more. Egg wash, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 190C for 50 minutes.

d.note: Fiery lemon, ginger and chilli topped with ginger beer
d.how: Blitz the juice of 3 lemons with a 5cm knob of grated ginger, 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of chopped red chilli, then strain. Divide between four glasses of ice and top each with about 150ml very cold ginger beer.

s.note: Crisp fried pasta shells in chilli salt, three each
s.how: Boil 150g conchiglie for 8 minutes, drain and dry well on a tea towel. Fry at 180C in batches until crisp and golden. Toss with flaky salt and chilli flakes while hot. Serve three per person to start, then the rest.

s.n: Future fast food chips and salsa
s.note: Fried corn tortilla chips with roasted tomato salsa
s.how: Cut 12 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C until crisp, then salt. Char 4 tomatoes, half an onion, 2 garlic cloves and a jalapeño under the grill. Blitz with the juice of a lime and salt. Serve in a bowl.

m.note: Big chuck burger with fried onions, cheddar and barbecue sauce
m.how: Shape 800g chuck mince into 4 thick patties and sear hard on a hot grill for 4 minutes a side. Fry 2 sliced onions until golden. Melt a slice of cheddar on each patty and stack on toasted buns with onions and barbecue sauce.

w.note: Three-layer jelly set in a slab and cut into perfect cubes
w.how: Make 3 packets of different coloured jelly crystals one at a time, using 2 gelatine leaves extra in each with 400ml water. Set each layer for an hour before adding the next. Turn out, cut into neat cubes and serve on a white plate with a little whipped cream.

d.n: Fizzy water in a fancy glass
d.note: Sparkling water with cucumber, mint and elderflower in a coupe
d.how: Put a few thin cucumber ribbons and a mint leaf in each of four coupes. Add 1 tsp elderflower cordial to each and top with chilled sparkling water, about 150ml per glass. Sip it like it's the future.

s.note: Golden cast iron cornbread straight from the oven
s.how: Heat a buttered cast iron pan in a 200C oven. Whisk 150g cornmeal, 100g flour, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 250ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 60g melted butter. Pour into the hot pan and bake 20 minutes. Serve warm with butter.

s.note: Thick chips with a cup of gravy for dipping
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips. Fry at 140C for 6 minutes, rest, then at 185C until crisp, and salt. Cook 30g butter with 2 tbsp flour for 2 minutes, then whisk in 400ml beef stock and simmer until thick. Serve the gravy in cups.

m.note: Double patty burger with cheddar, bacon, fried egg and lettuce
m.how: Shape 1kg beef mince into 8 patties and grill. Fry 8 rashers of bacon and 4 eggs. Stack two patties on each toasted bun with cheddar, the bacon, a fried egg and shredded iceberg. Serve with plenty of napkins.

w.note: Vanilla slab cake piped with a blue police badge
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 200g sugar, add 4 eggs and fold in 250g self-raising flour and 125ml milk. Bake in a slab tin at 175C for 30 minutes. Beat 200g butter with 350g icing sugar, spread on and pipe a badge and Graduates in blue.

d.note: Fresh lemonade over ice with mint
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Stir with the juice of 5 lemons and 1L cold water. Pour over ice in four tall glasses and add a sprig of mint and a lemon slice to each.

s.note: Smoked salmon on buttered rye with crème fraîche and dill
s.how: Butter 6 slices rye bread and cut into small squares. Top each with a fold of smoked salmon, using 200g in total, a small spoon of crème fraîche, a dill sprig and a crack of black pepper. Serve cold on a tray.

s.note: Ripe peach wedges with warm honey, lime and mint
s.how: Cut 4 ripe peaches into wedges and arrange on a plate. Warm 2 tbsp honey with the juice of a lime and drizzle over. Scatter with torn mint and a small pinch of flaky salt. Serve straight away.

m.note: Garlic butter lobster tails with a sharp green salad
m.how: Split 4 lobster tails lengthways. Brush with 80g butter melted with 2 garlic cloves and chopped parsley. Grill flesh side up for 6 to 8 minutes until just white. Toss salad leaves with a lemon and olive oil vinaigrette and serve alongside.

w.note: Warm cinnamon peaches under a buttery biscuit topping
w.how: Toss 6 sliced peaches with 80g sugar, lemon juice and 1 tsp cinnamon in a baking dish. Rub 80g butter into 200g self-raising flour, stir in 150ml buttermilk and drop spoonfuls over the fruit. Bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

d.note: Brut champagne, chilled and poured into flutes
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of brut champagne in an ice bucket with ice and water for 30 minutes. Open it gently so it hisses rather than pops. Pour slowly into four flutes and let the foam settle before topping up.

s.note: Cheddar, pork pie, pickles, apple and crusty bread on a board
s.how: Take 250g mature cheddar out of the fridge an hour ahead and cut into thick slices. Cut a pork pie into wedges. Arrange on a board with pickled onions, chutney, a sliced apple, crusty bread and a dish of salted butter.

s.note: Jammy scotch eggs in crisp panko with English mustard
s.how: Boil 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Wrap each in 100g seasoned sausage mince. Roll in flour, 1 beaten egg and 100g panko. Fry at 170C for 7 minutes, halve and serve with English mustard.

m.note: Beef and ale pie under puff pastry with chips and peas
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, add 2 onions, thyme, 375ml ale and a dash of Worcestershire and braise 2.5 hours. Thicken and pour into a pie dish. Cover with puff, bake at 200C for 25 minutes. Serve with chips and 300g peas.

w.note: Strawberry ripple cones dipped in chocolate and nuts
w.how: Blitz 250g strawberries with 2 tbsp sugar. Soften 1L vanilla ice cream and ripple the strawberry sauce through, then refreeze. Dip the rims of 4 waffle cones in 100g melted dark chocolate and chopped peanuts. Fill with scoops and freeze until serving.

d.note: Cranberry juice in a pint glass, ale for everyone else
d.how: Pour 500ml cold cranberry juice into a pint glass for the designated driver, no ice. For everyone else, pour three 500ml bottles of English ale into pint glasses. Raise them for the greater good.

s.note: Homemade peanut butter buttons dipped in bright candy coating
s.how: Beat 200g peanut butter with 100g icing sugar and 30g soft butter. Roll into small discs and chill 30 minutes. Dip in 250g melted coloured candy melts and set on baking paper. Lay them in a trail across the table.

s.note: Cheddar crackers cut into little letters
s.how: Pulse 150g grated cheddar, 60g cold butter and 100g flour with salt until it forms a dough, adding a splash of water. Roll thin and cut into letters with small cutters. Bake at 180C for 12 minutes until crisp.

m.note: Pepperoni pizza cut into squares for the whole family
m.how: Stretch 500g pizza dough into 2 thin bases. Spread with pizza sauce and top with 250g mozzarella and 100g pepperoni. Bake on a steel or tray at the oven's highest heat for 7 to 8 minutes, then cut into squares.

w.note: Milk chocolate cups with a soft peanut butter middle
w.how: Melt 300g milk chocolate. Spoon a little into 12 cupcake liners and chill. Mix 150g peanut butter with 50g icing sugar and put a spoon on each. Cover with the rest of the chocolate and chill until set.

d.note: Root beer over ice, or as a float
d.how: Pour four 375ml cans of root beer over ice into tall glasses. For a float, skip the ice and add a scoop of vanilla ice cream, then pour slowly so it foams up. Long spoons and straws.

s.note: Hot salted peanuts in paper bags
s.how: Spread 400g peanuts in the shell on a tray and roast at 180C for 20 minutes. Toss with a teaspoon of fine salt while still hot. Divide between four paper bags and leave an empty bowl for the shells.

s.note: Salted soft pretzels with a warm cheese sauce
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with butter, sprinkle with coarse salt and warm at 200C for 5 minutes. Heat 375ml evaporated milk and stir in 200g grated cheddar until smooth. Serve the sauce warm in a bowl for dunking.

m.note: Franks smothered in beef chilli, cheddar and onion
m.how: Brown 400g beef mince with 1 onion and 2 tsp chilli powder, add 1 tin tomatoes and simmer 45 minutes. Griddle 8 franks. Put in steamed buns, spoon over chilli and top with 100g grated cheddar and diced onion.

w.note: Vanilla ice cream cups rippled with chocolate sauce
w.how: Soften 1L vanilla ice cream for 5 minutes. Swirl through 100ml chocolate sauce and spoon into four paper cups. Refreeze for an hour. Serve with little wooden spoons like at the ballpark.

d.note: Cold lager in plastic cups, passed down the row
d.how: Chill eight 355ml cans of American lager for at least three hours. Pour into plastic cups and pass them down the couch like you're in the stands. Try not to spill any on the person beside you.

s.note: Tiny fried quail eggs on brioche with bacon and chives
s.how: Toast 12 small rounds of brioche. Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp and break into pieces. Fry 12 quail eggs in 30g butter for a minute. Put an egg and a bit of bacon on each round and sprinkle with chives.

s.note: Thick chips with garlic aioli for dipping
s.how: Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140C for 6 minutes, rest, then at 185C until crisp. Whisk 1 yolk, 1 crushed garlic clove and lemon juice, then drip in 200ml oil until thick. Salt the chips and serve with the aioli.

m.note: Grilled rib eye and corn with creamy coleslaw
m.how: Grill 4 rib eyes and 4 corn cobs over high heat. Shred a quarter cabbage and 2 carrots and toss with 100g mayo, 2 tbsp cider vinegar, a pinch of sugar and salt. Rest the steaks 5 minutes and serve with the corn and slaw.

w.note: Vanilla custard tarts with nutmeg on top
w.how: Line a 12-hole muffin tray with rounds cut from 2 sheets sweet shortcrust and blind-bake. Whisk 3 eggs, 250ml milk, 125ml cream and 80g sugar. Fill the cases, grate nutmeg on top and bake at 150C for 20 minutes until just set.

d.note: Lager in frosted glasses, officers' club style
d.how: Put four glasses in the freezer for 30 minutes until frosted. Chill eight 355ml bottles of American lager. Pour into the frosted glasses and salute anyone who comes through the door.

s.note: Nuts, apricots, dark chocolate and pepitas for the climb
s.how: Toss 200g mixed nuts, 100g chopped dried apricots, 100g dark chocolate chunks and 50g pepitas with a pinch of sea salt. Divide into four zip bags or a big bowl. Keep it handy for the long haul.

s.note: Creamy roast pumpkin soup poured from a thermos
s.how: Roast 1kg diced pumpkin at 200C for 30 minutes. Soften 1 onion and 2 garlic cloves, add the pumpkin and 750ml stock and simmer 10 minutes. Blitz smooth, stir in 100ml cream and pour into a warmed thermos.

m.note: Rosemary rump grilled over coals with foil-baked potatoes
m.how: Wrap 4 potatoes with a knob of butter each in foil and bake in the coals for 45 minutes. Rub 4 rump steaks with salt, pepper and chopped rosemary. Grill over hot coals for 4 minutes a side and rest on a board.

w.note: Warm fudgy brownies with hot chocolate sauce
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 80g flour and 30g cocoa. Bake at 175C for 25 minutes. Melt 100g chocolate with 150ml cream and pour over the warm brownies at the table.

d.note: Frothy dark hot chocolate with a pinch of salt
d.how: Heat 1L milk until steaming. Whisk in 150g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of salt until melted and frothy. Pour into four mugs and drink while it's hot, wrapped in a blanket.

s.note: Loaded nachos with beans, cheese, guacamole and sour cream
s.how: Layer a 300g bag of corn chips with a drained tin of black beans, 200g cheddar and jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes. Mash 2 avocados with lime and salt. Top with a jar of salsa, the guacamole and 150g sour cream.

s.note: Parmesan meatballs in tomato sauce, on toothpicks
s.how: Mix 250g beef mince and 250g pork mince with 40g parmesan, chopped parsley and a crushed garlic clove. Roll into 24 balls and brown. Simmer in a tin of crushed tomatoes for 30 minutes. Serve on toothpicks.

m.note: Cheeseburgers with bacon and the works, plus fries
m.how: Shape 800g chuck mince into 4 patties and grill to medium. Fry 8 rashers of bacon. Build on toasted buns with cheddar, bacon, iceberg, tomato and pickles. Fry 1kg potatoes cut into fries, twice, and salt.

w.note: Fudge-frosted chocolate cake with a red ball on top
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 200g butter. Whisk in 4 eggs and 200g sugar, then fold in 150g self-raising flour. Bake at 170C for 40 minutes. Cover with fudge frosting of 300g icing sugar, 40g cocoa and 80g butter, and top with a red fondant ball.

d.note: Orange, lemon and honey with soda, a pinch of salt
d.how: Stir 500ml orange juice with the juice of 2 lemons, 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of fine salt until the honey dissolves. Pour over ice in four tall glasses and top each with soda water.

s.note: Black bean dip with feta, coriander and green chilli
s.how: Blitz 2 drained tins black beans with 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp cumin and the juice of 2 limes until smooth. Spread in a bowl and top with 80g crumbled feta, coriander and a sliced green chilli. Serve with corn chips.

s.note: Thin crisp green plantain chips with lime salt
s.how: Peel 3 green plantains and slice very thin on a mandoline. Fry at 175C in batches until crisp, about 2 minutes. Drain and toss straight away with flaky salt mixed with the zest of a lime.

m.note: Smoky paprika rump grilled hot, with sharp green chimichurri
m.how: Rub 4 rump steaks with salt, pepper and 2 tsp smoked paprika. Grill over high heat for 4 minutes a side and rest. Chop a bunch of parsley with 2 garlic cloves and mix with 3 tbsp red wine vinegar, 100ml oil and chilli flakes. Spoon over.

w.note: Dense chocolate mud cake with ganache dragged like mud
w.how: Melt 250g dark chocolate and 250g butter. Whisk in 4 eggs and 300g sugar, then fold in 150g flour and 30g cocoa. Bake at 160C for 70 minutes. Melt 150g chocolate with 150ml cream, pour over and drag with a fork.

d.note: Ice-cold Mexican lager with a lime in the neck
d.how: Bury eight 355ml bottles of Mexican lager in a cooler of ice for an hour. Push a lime wedge into the neck of each bottle and hand them out. Drink before anything in the trees moves.

s.note: Two bowls of popcorn, buttery and parmesan pepper
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil with 3 kernels, then add 150g kernels once they pop, cover and shake until popping slows. Toss half with 40g melted butter and salt, and half with 40g grated parmesan and cracked pepper. Keep it coming.

s.note: Food truck nachos with salsa, sour cream and guacamole
s.how: Layer a 300g bag of corn chips with a drained tin of black beans, 200g cheddar and jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes. Mash 2 avocados with lime and salt and spoon on with sour cream and a jar of salsa.

m.note: Smashed double cheeseburger with onions pressed in
m.how: Roll 800g beef mince into 8 balls. Put a few thin onion slices on each, then smash flat onion-side down on a hot griddle. Flip after 90 seconds, add American cheese and stack two per toasted bun with pickles and mustard.

w.note: Chocolate biscuit base, green peppermint cream, dark chocolate top
w.how: Crush 250g chocolate biscuits with 100g melted butter and press into a tin. Beat 300g icing sugar, 60g butter, 1 tsp peppermint essence, a splash of milk and green colouring and spread on. Cover with 150g melted dark chocolate and chill.

d.note: Fresh lemon squash topped with soda water
d.how: Dissolve 120g sugar in 120ml hot water and cool. Mix with the juice of 4 lemons. Divide between four glasses of ice and top each with about 200ml soda water. Stir and add a slice of lemon.

s.note: Cinnamon sugar pretzels with cream cheese icing to dip
s.how: Brush 4 soft pretzels with 40g melted butter and roll in 80g caster sugar mixed with 2 tsp cinnamon. Warm at 200C for 5 minutes. Beat 125g cream cheese with 60g icing sugar and a splash of milk for dipping.

s.note: Warm folded tortillas with refried beans, cheese and salsa
s.how: Warm 8 flour tortillas on a hot dry pan. Spread with a tin of refried beans, sprinkle with 150g cheddar and add a spoon of salsa made from 2 diced tomatoes and a chopped jalapeño. Fold and warm again until the cheese melts.

m.note: Grilled skirt steak tacos with salsa roja
m.how: Marinate 800g skirt steak in lime, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tsp cumin for 2 hours. Soak 3 dried chillies, blitz with a tomato and garlic for salsa roja. Grill the steak hot, slice and serve in 16 corn tortillas with onion and coriander.

w.note: Vanilla panna cotta brushed with silver lustre
w.how: Soak 3 gelatine leaves. Warm 400ml cream, 200ml milk, 80g sugar and a split vanilla bean until steaming, then stir in the gelatine. Pour into 4 moulds and set overnight. Turn out and brush with edible silver lustre.

d.note: Blue raspberry slushies blitzed with lots of ice
d.how: Blitz 200ml blue raspberry cordial with 600ml cold water and 4 cups of ice until smooth and slushy. Pour into four cups and serve straight away with spoon straws before it melts.

s.note: Spiral curly fries with smoked paprika salt
s.how: Spiralise 4 large potatoes and soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Dry very well on tea towels. Fry at 180C in batches until crisp and golden. Toss with fine salt mixed with 1 tsp smoked paprika and serve hot.

s.note: Pink hoverboard tortilla chips with guacamole
s.how: Cut 6 flour tortillas into hoverboard shapes. Fry at 180C until crisp and toss with salt and 1 tsp beetroot powder for a pink colour. Mash 3 avocados with the juice of a lime and salt for guacamole.

m.note: Thin New York pepperoni pizza after a quick mini pizza reveal
m.how: Bake 4 mini pizza bases with sauce and cheese for the reveal. Then stretch 500g dough thin, spread with 200g crushed tomatoes, add 250g low-moisture mozzarella and 100g pepperoni, and bake on a hot steel at max heat for 7 minutes.

w.note: Blue jelly with gummy sharks swimming in it
w.how: Make 2 packets blue jelly crystals with 500ml boiling and 500ml cold water. Pour halfway into four glasses and chill until just starting to set. Push in gummy sharks, add the rest of the jelly and set. Top with whipped cream waves.

d.note: Thick strawberry milkshake with fresh strawberries
d.how: For each shake, blend 3 scoops strawberry ice cream with 4 strawberries and 150ml cold milk until thick. Pour into a tall chilled glass with a straw. Make four one after the other so they stay thick.

s.note: Mini sandwiches wrapped in paper with names written on
s.how: Boil 3 eggs, mash with mayo. Make ham, cheese and pickle sandwiches, and egg and lettuce sandwiches, using 12 slices white bread, 100g ham and 100g cheddar. Cut small, wrap each in baking paper and write a name on it in marker.

s.note: Crisp cheddar pastry stars with a pinch of paprika
s.how: Rub 80g butter into 150g flour, then add 120g grated vintage cheddar and a pinch of paprika. Bring together with a splash of water. Roll thin, cut into stars, brush with egg and bake at 180C for 12 minutes until golden.

m.note: Pepperoni pizza with a drizzle of chilli honey
m.how: Stretch 500g dough into 2 thin bases. Spread with 200g crushed tomatoes and top with 250g mozzarella and 100g pepperoni. Bake on a hot steel at max heat for 7 minutes. Warm 3 tbsp honey with chilli flakes and drizzle over.

w.note: Guitar sugar cookies iced red, black and white
w.how: Beat 125g butter with 100g sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour. Roll out, cut into guitar shapes and bake at 180C for 8 minutes. Mix 300g icing sugar with egg white and a little water, colour some red and black, and decorate.

d.note: Pineapple and orange punch with lemonade in a big jug
d.how: Pour 500ml pineapple juice and 500ml orange juice into a big jug with plenty of ice. Top with 750ml cold lemonade and add a sliced orange. Stir gently and pour into four glasses.

s.note: Cold sesame noodles with chilli oil and cucumber
s.how: Cook 400g fresh wheat noodles, rinse cold and drain. Whisk 3 tbsp sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp chilli oil and a crushed garlic clove. Toss through and top with cucumber matchsticks and spring onion.

s.note: Seeded crackers with lemon cream cheese and smoked oysters
s.how: Whip 150g cream cheese with the zest of a lemon. Spread on 16 seeded crackers and top each with a smoked oyster from 2 drained tins. Finish with cracked pepper and snipped chives. Serve straight away.

m.note: Pork and vegetable noodle stir-fry in bowls
m.how: Slice 500g pork shoulder thin and toss with soy. Stir-fry in a smoking wok, then add a quarter cabbage, 2 carrots and 1 capsicum, all sliced, with grated ginger. Add 400g egg noodles, 3 tbsp oyster sauce and 2 tbsp soy, toss and serve in bowls.

w.note: Red velvet dome that bursts with raspberry jam when cut
w.how: Beat 125g butter and 250g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 250ml buttermilk, 1 tsp vinegar and red colouring. Bake in a bowl at 170C for 50 minutes. Hollow, fill with raspberry jam and cover in cream cheese frosting.

d.note: Drip coffee with milk and sugar before the signal
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine. Pour into four mugs and leave milk and sugar on the table for everyone. Drink it before anyone goes to check on a distress signal.

s.note: Smoky red capsicum and walnut dip with warm flatbread
s.how: Roast 3 red capsicums until black, peel and seed. Blitz with 100g toasted walnuts, 2 tbsp pomegranate molasses, a garlic clove, 1 tsp cumin and a pinch of chilli. Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with oil and serve with warm flatbread.

s.note: Thin potato chips in red Mars dust seasoning
s.how: Slice 4 potatoes thin on a mandoline, rinse and dry well. Fry at 170C in batches until crisp. Toss straight away with 1 tbsp vinegar powder, 1 tsp sweet paprika and fine salt so they turn red like Mars dust.

m.note: Red lentil and capsicum stew with yoghurt
m.how: Soften 1 onion, 2 garlic cloves and 2 diced red capsicums. Add 1 tsp smoked paprika, 250g red lentils, 1 tin crushed tomatoes and 750ml stock and simmer 25 minutes until thick. Serve in bowls with a spoon of Greek yoghurt on top.

w.note: Red velvet cake with cream cheese frosting and red sugar
w.how: Beat 125g butter and 250g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 2 tbsp cocoa, 250ml buttermilk, 1 tsp vinegar and red colouring. Bake at 170C for 30 minutes. Frost with 250g cream cheese beaten with 200g icing sugar and dust with red sugar.

d.note: Cold gin martini with an olive
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml gin and 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds until very cold. Strain into a chilled martini glass and drop in a green olive on a pick. Makes four.

s.note: Little honey vanilla biscuits in animal shapes
s.how: Beat 125g butter with 80g sugar and 2 tbsp honey, then mix in 250g flour. Roll thin and cut with small animal cutters. Bake at 170C for 10 minutes until pale golden. Cool on a rack and pile into a bowl.

s.note: Twisted pretzel spirals like drill bits, with coarse salt
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g yeast, 300ml warm water and salt and prove an hour. Roll into long ropes and twist into spirals. Dip each for 30 seconds in simmering water with 3 tbsp bicarb, sprinkle with coarse salt and bake at 220C for 12 minutes.

m.note: Rib eye with buttery mash and onion gravy
m.how: Mash 1kg potatoes with 80g butter and milk. Cook 2 sliced onions in butter for 20 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp flour and add 400ml beef stock, then simmer. Sear 4 rib eyes hard, rest 5 minutes and pour the gravy over.

w.note: Animal biscuits dipped in pink and white with sprinkles
w.how: Make a batch of animal biscuits from 125g butter, 80g sugar and 250g flour, baked at 170C for 10 minutes. Dip each half into 250g melted pink or white candy melts and add sprinkles. Serve with a bowl of 300ml whipped cream.

d.note: Ice-cold lager in the bottle, one for every driller
d.how: Chill eight 355ml bottles of American lager for at least three hours, or in a bucket of ice for 30 minutes. Hand them out cold and toast the crew who made it home.

s.note: Corn tortilla chips with fresh corn and tomato salsa
s.how: Cut 12 corn tortillas into wedges and fry at 180C until crisp, then salt. Char 2 corn cobs and cut off the kernels. Mix with 3 diced tomatoes, chopped coriander and the juice of 2 limes. Serve the salsa in a bowl with the chips.

s.note: Grilled tinned peaches with honey yoghurt
s.how: Drain 2 tins of peach halves and pat dry. Grill cut side down in a hot pan for 3 minutes until caramelised. Serve warm with a spoon of Greek yoghurt mixed with honey, about 200g yoghurt in total.

m.note: Garlic and thyme basted sirloin, with a plain bit for the dog
m.how: Season 4 sirloins well and sear in a hot pan for 3 minutes a side. Add 50g butter, 2 crushed garlic cloves and thyme and baste for a minute. Rest 5 minutes and slice. Keep a plain unseasoned piece aside for the dog.

w.note: Brown sugar peaches under a buttermilk biscuit topping
w.how: Drain 2 tins sliced peaches and toss with 60g brown sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon in a baking dish. Rub 80g butter into 200g self-raising flour, stir in 150ml buttermilk and drop spoonfuls over the fruit. Bake at 190C for 35 minutes.

d.note: Bourbon neat, or bottled water for the long night
d.how: Pour 45ml bourbon neat into each of four tumblers. Put a few bottles of spring water on the bench for anyone who wants to keep a clear head. Lock the door before you pour.

s.note: Garlic parmesan breadsticks knotted into bones, with marinara
s.how: Roll 500g pizza dough into 12 ropes and knot both ends into bone shapes. Brush with 50g butter melted with 2 garlic cloves and sprinkle with 40g parmesan. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Simmer a tin of crushed tomatoes 10 minutes to dip.

s.note: Cold watermelon, feta and mint skewers with lime
s.how: Cut a quarter of a watermelon and 200g feta into cubes. Thread onto skewers with a mint leaf between. Squeeze over the juice of a lime and add a pinch of flaky salt just before serving very cold.

m.note: Cart franks with brown mustard, sauerkraut and red onion sauce
m.how: Soften 2 sliced onions in oil for 15 minutes, add 2 tbsp tomato paste and a splash of water and cook down. Simmer 8 franks in water for 5 minutes. Put in steamed buns with spicy mustard, warm sauerkraut and the onions.

w.note: Toasted banana bread slices spread with butter
w.how: Mash 3 ripe bananas with 100g melted butter, 150g brown sugar and 2 eggs. Fold in 250g flour and 1 tsp bicarb. Bake in a loaf tin at 170C for an hour. Cool, slice thick, toast and spread with butter.

d.note: Strong coffee with milk and sugar, sipped through the night
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water so it's strong. Stir in 200ml warm milk and sugar to taste. Pour into a thermos warmed with hot water first. Sip from the lid through the night shift.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork and cabbage gyoza with chilli dipping sauce
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with 2 cups finely shredded cabbage, salted and squeezed, plus soy and ginger. Fill 30 gyoza wrappers and pleat. Fry until crisp underneath, add water and steam with a lid for 4 minutes. Dip in soy, rice vinegar and chilli oil.

s.note: Puffed rice paper triangles with shichimi and salt
s.how: Cut 10 rice paper sheets into small triangles with scissors. Fry a few at a time at 180C for a few seconds until they puff and turn white. Drain and toss with flaky salt and a good shake of shichimi togarashi.

m.note: Soy-braised pork belly ramen with jammy eggs and nori
m.how: Braise 600g pork belly in 125ml soy, 125ml mirin, 125ml sake and 500ml water for 2 hours, then slice. Marinate 4 soft-boiled eggs in some of the liquid. Cook 4 serves ramen into 1.5L hot stock seasoned with soy. Top with pork, egg, nori and spring onion.

w.note: Thin sesame tuiles folded into shapes while hot
w.how: Whisk 2 egg whites with 100g sugar, then stir in 50g flour, 50g melted butter and 2 tbsp sesame seeds. Spread thin circles on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Fold or twist into shapes while still hot and soft.

d.note: Japanese whisky neat in a heavy glass, a drop of water
d.how: Pour 45ml Japanese whisky into each of four heavy tumblers. Add a single drop of water from a teaspoon to open it up. Sip slowly while the rain comes down outside.

s.note: Speckled brown butter cookies with a chocolate egg hidden inside
s.how: Brown 125g butter and cool. Beat with 150g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 225g flour. Wrap dough around 12 small chocolate eggs, shape into ovals and bake at 175C for 12 minutes. Flick with cocoa mixed with a little water for speckles.

s.note: Curved tortilla claws baked crisp with smoked paprika, guacamole
s.how: Cut 6 flour tortillas into curved claw shapes. Brush with oil, sprinkle with salt and smoked paprika and bake at 200C for 8 minutes until crisp. Mash 3 avocados with the juice of 2 limes and salt for guacamole.

m.note: Herb-crusted lamb rack with pea mint purée and baby potatoes
m.how: Brush 2 lamb racks with Dijon and press on chopped parsley and breadcrumbs. Roast at 220C until 55C inside, about 20 minutes, and rest. Boil 300g peas with mint and blitz with butter. Roast 800g baby potatoes. Slice and plate neatly.

w.note: Soft vanilla ice cream with hot fudge and crushed honeycomb
w.how: Melt 100g dark chocolate with 100ml cream for hot fudge. Leave 1L vanilla ice cream out for 10 minutes so it softens a little too much. Scoop three each into chilled coupes, pour over the fudge and scatter crushed honeycomb.

d.note: Iced sparkling water with lemon, set down to ripple
d.how: Fill four tall glasses with ice and lemon slices and top with chilled sparkling water. Set them on the table where everyone can see them, and keep an eye on the surface for ripples.

s.note: Baked buttery nuts and pretzels with garlic
s.how: Toss 300g mixed nuts and 150g pretzels with 50g melted butter, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 1 tsp garlic powder. Spread on a tray and bake at 140C for 30 minutes, stirring twice. Cool and serve in bowls.

s.note: Jagged cracker shards with a coarse olive tapenade
s.how: Pulse 200g pitted black olives with 1 tbsp capers, 3 anchovies, a garlic clove, lemon juice and 3 tbsp olive oil until coarse. Break a packet of seeded crackers into jagged shards and serve with the tapenade.

m.note: Beef and bean chilli with sour cream and cheddar
m.how: Brown 800g beef mince with 1 onion and 2 tbsp chilli powder. Add 2 tins crushed tomatoes and 2 drained tins kidney beans and simmer 90 minutes until thick. Serve in bowls topped with sour cream and grated cheddar.

w.note: Fudgy dark chocolate brownies pulled while still wobbly
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter. Whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 80g flour and 30g cocoa. Bake in a lined tin at 175C for 25 minutes, pulling it out while the centre still wobbles. Cool before cutting.

d.note: Blue raspberry cordial with lemonade and a lemon wheel
d.how: Fill four tall glasses with plenty of ice. Add 40ml blue raspberry cordial to each and top with about 200ml cold lemonade. Stir and add a lemon wheel to each glass.

s.note: Thin golden fries with sauce in a squeeze bottle
s.how: Cut 1kg russets into thin fries and soak for 30 minutes, then dry well. Fry at 140C for 5 minutes, rest, then at 190C until golden. Salt straight away and serve with tomato sauce in a squeeze bottle.

s.note: Baked nachos with refried beans, cheddar and jalapeños
s.how: Spread a 300g bag of corn chips on a tray and dot with a tin of refried beans. Scatter with 200g grated cheddar and sliced jalapeños. Bake at 200C for 8 minutes and top with sour cream and a jar of salsa.

m.note: Classic diner cheeseburger with the works
m.how: Shape 800g chuck mince into 4 thick patties, season just before cooking and griddle to medium. Melt cheddar on top under a lid. Build on toasted buns with shredded iceberg, sliced tomato, onion and pickles.

w.note: Lattice-topped cherry pie, the slice everyone at the diner orders
w.how: Toss 800g pitted cherries, fresh or frozen, with 150g sugar, the juice of a lemon and 3 tbsp cornflour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice from 2 more. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes.

d.note: Drip coffee in diner mugs, milk and sugar on the table
d.how: Brew 60g ground coffee with 1L water in a drip machine. Pour into heavy diner mugs and leave a jug of milk and the sugar bowl on the table. Refill whenever a mug is half empty.

s.note: Homemade chocolate bars, one hiding a golden ticket
s.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and 100g milk chocolate gently and pour into 4 bar moulds. Sprinkle a little flaky salt on top and set in the fridge for an hour. Wrap each in paper, slipping a gold foil ticket under one wrapper.

s.note: Cinnamon-candied walnuts, pecans and almonds, roasted until crunchy and sticky
s.how: Whisk 1 egg white until frothy, then toss with 100g each of walnuts, pecans and almonds. Coat in 80g brown sugar, 1 tsp cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Roast at 160C for 20 minutes, stirring twice, then cool and break apart.

m.note: Bratwurst with wine-braised sauerkraut, mustard and pretzels
m.how: Simmer a 500g jar of sauerkraut with 125ml white wine and 1 tsp caraway for 20 minutes. Grill 8 bratwurst slowly until browned all over. Warm 4 soft pretzels. Serve together with plenty of wholegrain mustard.

w.note: Lattice blueberry pie with vanilla ice cream
w.how: Toss 750g blueberries with 150g sugar, the juice of a lemon and 3 tbsp cornflour. Line a pie dish with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust, fill and weave a lattice from 2 more. Bake at 190C for 50 minutes, cool 3 hours and serve with ice cream.

d.note: Frothy hot chocolate of dark and milk chocolate
d.how: Heat 800ml milk and 200ml cream until steaming. Whisk in 100g dark chocolate and 50g milk chocolate, chopped, and keep whisking hard until it's thick and frothy like the waterfall. Pour into four mugs.

s.note: Chocolate pretzel rods striped plaid with candy melts
s.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate and dip 20 pretzel rods two-thirds of the way. Set on baking paper. Melt 100g coloured candy melts, pipe stripes across in two directions for a plaid pattern and let them set.

s.note: Honey butter mix of cereal, pretzels, peanuts and marshmallows
s.how: Toss 150g cereal squares, 100g pretzels and 100g peanuts with 50g butter melted with 2 tbsp honey. Bake at 140C for 20 minutes, stirring once. Cool completely, then toss through 100g mini marshmallows.

m.note: Molten deep pan four-cheese pepperoni pizza
m.how: Press 600g pizza dough into an oiled deep tray and prove 30 minutes. Spread with a jar of pizza sauce and pile on 200g mozzarella, 100g provolone, 50g parmesan, 100g cheddar and 100g pepperoni. Bake at 220C for 20 minutes until molten.

w.note: Honey vanilla yoghurt layered with granola and berries
w.how: Whip 500g Greek yoghurt with 3 tbsp honey and a little vanilla. Layer in four tall glasses with 200g granola and 250g mixed berries, finishing with berries on top. Serve straight away so the granola stays crunchy.

d.note: Sparkling water poured from the can like it's precious
d.how: Chill four 375ml cans of sparkling water. Fill four glasses with ice and a twist of lime. Open each can slowly, take a deep breath of it, then pour with great ceremony.

s.note: One giant rice bubble ring to share
s.how: Melt 60g butter with 250g marshmallows over low heat. Stir through 150g puffed rice cereal until coated. Press firmly into a greased ring mould and set for an hour. Turn out and cut into wedges at the table.

s.note: Two big chocolate cookies sandwiched with thick vanilla cream
s.how: Beat 100g soft butter with 200g icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla until fluffy. Spread thickly between two large dark chocolate cookies, about 20cm across, pressing gently. Chill 20 minutes and cut into wedges.

m.note: One huge buttermilk pancake cut into wedges
m.how: Whisk 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp sugar, 500ml buttermilk and 2 eggs. Pour into a large buttered pan over low heat, cover and cook 8 minutes, then flip with a plate and cook 5 more. Cut into wedges with butter and maple syrup.

w.note: A giant choc chip cookie baked in a pizza tray
w.how: Beat 150g soft butter with 200g brown sugar and 1 egg. Mix in 250g flour, half a tsp bicarb and 200g choc chips. Press into a pizza tray and bake at 180C for 18 minutes until golden at the edges and soft in the middle.

d.note: Fresh lemonade over ice, backyard style
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Stir with the juice of 5 lemons and 1L cold water in a big jug. Pour over ice in four glasses and drink it out on the lawn.

s.note: Garlic butter rump cubes with a peppercorn dip
s.how: Cut 600g rump into cubes and season well. Sear hard in a smoking pan in batches, then toss with 40g butter and 2 crushed garlic cloves. Mix 150g sour cream with 1 tsp cracked peppercorns. Serve the bites on toothpicks with the dip.

s.note: Long thin lavash crackers dusted with bright green herb salt
s.how: Blitz a handful of parsley and dill with 2 tbsp flaky salt until green. Brush 3 lavash breads with oil, sprinkle with the herb salt and cut into long thin strips. Bake at 180C for 8 minutes until crisp.

m.note: Butter-basted sirloin with red wine sauce
m.how: Dry-brine 4 sirloins overnight. Sear hard, then baste with 50g butter and thyme for a minute and rest. Add 125ml red wine and 250ml stock to the pan and reduce by half, then whisk in a knob of butter. Slice the steak and pour over.

w.note: Brown butter choc chip cookies with flaky salt
w.how: Brown 150g butter and cool. Beat with 200g brown sugar and 1 egg, then mix in 250g flour, half a tsp bicarb and 200g choc chips. Rest overnight. Roll into 16 balls and bake at 180C for 10 minutes. Sprinkle with flaky salt.

d.note: Two jugs, cranberry soda or blue lemonade, your choice
d.how: Fill one jug with 500ml cranberry juice and 500ml soda water over ice. Fill the other with 100ml blue raspberry cordial and 900ml soda water. Offer each guest the choice and see who picks which.

s.note: Buttery popcorn with a heavy cheese powder dusting
s.how: Pop 120g kernels in 2 tbsp oil. Toss with 50g melted butter, then 4 tbsp cheddar cheese powder, 1 tsp smoked paprika and a pinch of salt until every piece is orange. Serve in a big bowl.

s.note: Smoked salmon rye and whipped feta cucumber cups
s.how: Butter 4 slices rye bread, cut into squares and top with 150g smoked salmon, crème fraîche and dill. Cut 2 cucumbers into thick rounds, scoop a little hollow and fill with 150g feta whipped with a splash of olive oil.

m.note: Franks with loose coney chilli, mustard and diced onion
m.how: Brown 300g beef mince with half a diced onion, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp cumin. Add 200ml water and simmer 20 minutes until loose. Griddle 8 franks, put in steamed buns and top with chilli, mustard and diced white onion.

w.note: Chocolate cupcakes under a torched mushroom-cloud meringue
w.how: Beat 125g butter and 150g sugar, add 2 eggs, then fold in 175g self-raising flour, 30g cocoa and 125ml milk. Bake 12 cupcakes at 180C for 18 minutes. Whisk 3 whites and 150g sugar over hot water, beat to stiff peaks, pipe tall and torch.

d.note: Ice-cold American lager straight from the can
d.how: Chill eight 375ml cans of American lager for at least three hours, or in a bucket of ice and water for 30 minutes. Hand them out and drink straight from the can, no glasses.

s.note: Spiced dark hot chocolate in tiny cups
s.how: Heat 500ml milk with a split red chilli and a cinnamon stick and steep 5 minutes off the heat. Strain, reheat and whisk in 120g chopped dark chocolate and a pinch of flaky salt until smooth. Pour into tiny cups.

s.note: Dark ganache truffles rolled in cocoa, hazelnuts or chilli sugar
s.how: Heat 150ml cream until steaming and pour over 250g chopped dark chocolate with 20g butter. Stir smooth and chill 3 hours. Scoop and roll into balls, then coat in cocoa, chopped toasted hazelnuts or sugar mixed with chilli flakes.

m.note: Confit duck legs with duck fat potatoes and salad
m.how: Salt 4 duck legs overnight with thyme and garlic. Rinse, then cook slowly in their own fat at 140C for 2.5 hours. Roast 1kg potatoes in some of the fat at 200C. Crisp the legs skin side down and serve with a green salad.

w.note: Dark chocolate mousse with a little chilli salt
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 30g butter. Whisk in 4 yolks, then fold in 4 whites whipped with 40g sugar. Spoon into small cups and chill 4 hours. Finish with a pinch of flaky salt mixed with chilli flakes.

d.note: Light French red in short tumblers, village style
d.how: Open a 750ml bottle of light southern French red half an hour before dinner to let it breathe. Pour into short tumblers rather than wine glasses, about 150ml each, the way they would in the village.

s.note: Devilled eggs with salmon roe and prosciutto asparagus
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes and halve. Mash the yolks with 3 tbsp mayo and 1 tsp Dijon, pipe back and top with salmon roe. Blanch a bunch of asparagus and wrap each spear in half a slice of prosciutto.

s.note: Bright yellow gruyère choux puffs, as loud as the coat
s.how: Bring 125ml water and 50g butter to the boil, beat in 75g flour and cook a minute. Cool slightly, beat in 2 eggs, then 80g grated gruyère and a pinch of turmeric. Pipe small mounds and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Spaghetti and meatballs in San Marzano tomato sauce
m.how: Mix 600g pork and beef mince with 2 slices bread soaked in milk, 1 egg and 40g parmesan. Roll into balls and brown. Simmer an hour in 2 tins San Marzano tomatoes with basil. Toss with 500g spaghetti and more parmesan.

w.note: Tall torched meringue over sharp lemon curd
w.how: Blind-bake a tin lined with 2 sheets sweet shortcrust. Cook the juice and zest of 3 lemons, 150g sugar, 3 tbsp cornflour and 250ml water until thick, then beat in 3 yolks and 50g butter. Fill, top with 3 whites whipped with 150g sugar and torch.

d.note: Stirred gin martini with a lemon twist
d.how: For each drink, stir 60ml gin and 10ml dry vermouth over plenty of ice for 30 seconds. Strain into a chilled martini glass and twist a strip of lemon peel over the top. Makes four.

s.note: Saucer-shaped meringues with lemon curd underneath
s.how: Whisk 3 egg whites and 180g sugar over simmering water until hot, then beat to stiff peaks. Pipe into flat saucer shapes with a small dome in the middle. Bake at 100C for 90 minutes and cool. Spread a dot of lemon curd underneath.

s.note: Tall seven-layer dip built in a glass, with corn chips
s.how: Layer in a tall glass bowl: a tin of refried beans, guacamole from 2 avocados, 200g sour cream, 2 diced tomatoes, 100g grated cheddar, sliced black olives and spring onion. Serve with corn chips.

m.note: A tall mountain of buttery mash under onion gravy
m.how: Boil 1.5kg floury potatoes, rice them and beat with 200ml hot milk and 100g butter. Cook 2 sliced onions slowly in butter, stir in a tablespoon of flour and add 400ml beef stock. Pile the mash into a tall mountain and pour gravy over.

w.note: Tall chocolate cake with ridges dragged in the frosting
w.how: Beat 200g butter and 250g sugar, add 4 eggs, then fold in 250g self-raising flour, 50g cocoa and 200ml milk. Bake in three small tins at 170C for 30 minutes. Stack tall with buttercream of 200g butter, 350g icing sugar and 40g cocoa, then drag ridges with a fork.

d.note: Fresh lemonade in a big kitchen jug
d.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Squeeze in the juice of 5 lemons and top up with 1L cold water in a big jug with ice. Pour into four glasses at the kitchen table.

s.note: Long sausage rolls cut like worms
s.how: Mix 500g pork sausage mince with 1 grated onion and chopped thyme. Lay along 2 sheets puff pastry, roll into long logs and egg wash. Bake at 200C for 25 minutes until deep golden. Cut into long pieces and serve with sauce.

s.note: Jerky, peanuts, pork rinds and pickled eggs on the counter
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 10 minutes, peel and pack into a jar with 250ml hot white vinegar, salt and a pinch of sugar, and chill overnight. Tip 100g jerky, 150g salted peanuts and a bag of pork rinds into bowls beside the jar.

m.note: Grilled rump and snags with molasses beans and coleslaw
m.how: Simmer 2 tins baked beans with a diced onion and 2 tbsp molasses for 20 minutes. Shred a quarter cabbage and toss with 100g mayo and a splash of vinegar. Grill 2 rump steaks and 4 thick sausages over hot coals and slice to share.

w.note: Chocolate pudding with biscuit dirt and gummy worms
w.how: Whisk 600ml milk, 80g sugar, 3 tbsp cocoa and 3 tbsp cornflour in a pot over medium heat until thick. Pour into four cups and chill 2 hours. Top with 100g crushed chocolate biscuits and push gummy worms in so they poke out.

d.note: Ice-cold cans of lager from the esky
d.how: Fill an esky with a bag of ice and a little cold water and bury eight 375ml cans of American lager for an hour. Hand them out cold and stay off the ground.

s.note: Thin homemade crisps with green chilli salt
s.how: Slice 600g potatoes 1.5mm thick on a mandoline, rinse and dry well. Fry at 170C in batches until golden and crisp. Toss with fine salt and a little green chilli powder while hot.

s.note: White chocolate popcorn with red and blue sprinkles and popping candy
s.how: Pop 100g kernels and spread on a lined tray. Drizzle over 150g melted white chocolate and toss gently. Scatter with red and blue sprinkles and 2 packets of popping candy before it sets. Break into clusters.

m.note: Sticky ribs, charred corn and mustard potato salad
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp smoked paprika and garlic. Wrap and bake at 150C for 2.5 hours, then unwrap and glaze under a hot grill. Char 4 corn cobs. Toss 1kg boiled potatoes with Dijon, oil and vinegar.

w.note: Cream-covered slab cake decorated as a flag with berries
w.how: Put a slab sponge cake on a board. Whip 600ml cream with 2 tbsp icing sugar and spread over the top. Fill the top left corner with 125g blueberries for stars, and lay rows of halved strawberries, 500g in total, for stripes.

d.note: Lager buried in an esky of ice
d.how: Fill an esky with a bag of ice and some cold water. Bury eight 375ml cans of American lager for an hour. Hand them out cold and toast the Fourth of July.

s.note: Lacy golden parmesan crisps with black pepper
s.how: Grate 150g parmesan finely. Spoon into small rounds on a tray lined with baking paper, leaving space between. Bake at 190C for 6 minutes until lacy and golden. Crack black pepper over each and cool on the tray to crisp.

s.note: Crisp pork belly bites in a sticky chilli soy glaze
s.how: Roast 800g pork belly cubes at 150C for 2 hours, then crisp at 230C for 15 minutes. Simmer 3 tbsp soy, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp black vinegar and chilli flakes until sticky. Toss through and scatter with sesame seeds.

m.note: Red wine braised short ribs over creamy polenta
m.how: Brown 2kg beef short ribs, add 375ml red wine, 500ml stock, 4 garlic cloves and thyme. Braise covered at 150C for 4 hours. Reduce the sauce until glossy. Cook 200g polenta in 1L water with butter and parmesan and spoon the ribs over.

w.note: Peanut butter shortbread bones half dipped in chocolate
w.how: Beat 100g butter with 100g peanut butter and 80g icing sugar, then mix in 200g flour. Roll out, cut into small bone shapes and bake at 170C for 12 minutes. Cool and half dip in 100g melted dark chocolate. Human food only.

d.note: Bourbon neat in a heavy glass, one big cube if you must
d.how: Pour 60ml bourbon into each of four heavy glasses. Offer a single large ice cube to anyone who wants it. Sip it slowly at the bar, and don't do business on the premises.

s.note: Coconut prawns and plantain chips on a silver tray
s.how: Dip 400g peeled green prawns in flour, beaten egg and a mix of 60g shredded coconut and 60g panko. Fry at 180C for 2 minutes. Slice 2 green plantains thin and fry until crisp. Serve both with sweet chilli.

s.note: Bright green gruyère choux puffs with basil and spinach
s.how: Blitz a handful of basil and spinach with 2 tbsp water. Boil 125ml water with 50g butter, beat in 75g flour and cook a minute. Cool, beat in 2 eggs, the green purée and 80g gruyère. Pipe and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

m.note: Garlic butter rump with double-fried chips
m.how: Fry 1kg potatoes cut into chips, first at 140C, then at 185C until crisp. Sear 4 rump steaks hard and rest. Mash 60g butter with 2 crushed garlic cloves and put a slice on each steak. Save the trimmings for the dog.

w.note: Lime custard pie on a biscuit crust with cream
w.how: Press 200g crushed biscuits mixed with 80g melted butter into a pie tin. Whisk 395g condensed milk with 4 yolks, the zest of 2 limes and 125ml lime juice. Bake at 160C for 15 minutes, chill overnight and top with 300ml whipped cream.

d.note: Green melon and vodka cocktail with an umbrella
d.how: For each drink, fill a tall glass with ice and add 30ml melon liqueur, 30ml vodka and a squeeze of lime. Top with about 120ml lemonade, stir and add a cocktail umbrella. Makes four.

s.note: Shaved ice soaked with homemade blue raspberry syrup
s.how: Simmer 250g raspberries with 150g sugar and 100ml water for 10 minutes, strain and cool, then add a drop of blue colouring. Pack shaved or crushed ice into four cups and pour the syrup over.

s.note: Baked spinach and artichoke dip with corn chips
s.how: Wilt 250g spinach, squeeze dry and chop. Mix with a jar of chopped marinated artichokes, 250g cream cheese, 100g sour cream and 50g grated parmesan. Top with 100g mozzarella and bake at 190C for 20 minutes. Serve with corn chips.

m.note: Beef Wellington with mushroom duxelles and prosciutto
